A state accompanied by initial application and sustained application is a condition, by way of root condition, for a state accompanied by initial application and sustained application. Roots accompanied by initial application and sustained application are a condition, by way of root condition, for their associated aggregates. At the moment of rebirth-linking … [and so forth] … *Vibhaṅgavāra, Hetu-paccaya: A state with initial application and sustained application is a condition, through the relation of root, for a state with initial application and sustained application—the roots with initial application and sustained application are a condition, through the relation of root, for the associated aggregates. At the moment of rebirth-linking … etc.*

A state with applied thought and sustained thought (*savitakkasavicāra*) is related to a state without applied thought but with sustained thought (*avitakkavicāramatta*) by way of the root condition (*hetupaccaya*): roots with applied thought and sustained thought are related to applied thought by way of the root condition. At the moment of rebirth-linking (*paṭisandhi*) … [etc] … A state with applied thought and sustained thought is related to a state without applied thought and sustained thought (*avitakkaavicāra*) by way of the root condition:

roots with applied thought and sustained thought are related to mind-produced matter (*cittasamuṭṭhāna-rūpa*) by way of the root condition. At the moment of rebirth-linking, roots with applied thought and sustained thought … [etc] …
Roots are related to kamma-produced matter by way of root condition.

A state with applied thought and sustained thought is related to a state with applied thought and sustained thought, and to a state without applied thought and sustained thought, by way of root condition:
roots with applied thought and sustained thought are related to their associated aggregates and to mind-originated matter.

It is a condition for material phenomena by way of the root-condition (*hetu-paccaya*). At the moment of rebirth-linking (*paṭisandhi*), roots accompanied by initial application and sustained application (*savitakka-savicāra*) are a condition by way of the root-condition for the associated aggregates and for the matter produced by kamma (*kaṭattā-rūpa*).

A state accompanied by initial application and sustained application is [a condition] for a state without initial application but with sustained application alone, and for a state without initial application and sustained application.
Condition by way of root condition: roots accompanied by applied thought and sustained thought are a condition for applied thought and for mind-produced matter by way of root condition.
At the moment of rebirth-linking, roots accompanied by applied thought and sustained thought are a condition for applied thought and for kamma-produced matter by way of root condition.

A state with applied thought and sustained thought is a condition, by way of root-condition, for a state with applied thought and sustained thought and for a state without applied thought but with sustained thought:
roots with applied thought and sustained thought are a condition, by way of root-condition, for their associated aggregates and for applied thought.
At the moment of rebirth-linking, roots with applied thought and sustained thought [are a condition] for their associated...
The aggregates and applied thought are related to [their concomitants] by way of root-condition.

A state with applied thought and sustained thought is related to a state with applied thought and sustained thought, to a state without applied thought but with sustained thought only, and to a state without applied thought and sustained thought by way of root-condition:
roots with applied thought and sustained thought are related to their associated aggregates...

And it is a condition for applied thought (*vitakka*) and for the material phenomena (*rūpa*) originated by consciousness by way of the root-condition (*hetu-paccaya*). At the moment of rebirth-linking (*paṭisandhi*),

roots accompanied by applied thought and sustained thought (*savitakka-savicāra*) are a condition by way of the root-condition for the associated aggregates (*khandha*), for applied thought, and for the material phenomena produced by karma (*kaṭattā-rūpa*).

A state consisting of non-initial application and sustained application is a condition for a state consisting of non-initial application and sustained application by way of the root-condition (*hetu-paccaya*).

Roots consisting of non-initial application and sustained application are a condition for their associated aggregates (*khandha*) by way of the root-condition. At the moment of rebirth-linking (*paṭisandhi*), roots consisting of non-initial application and sustained application are a condition for their associated aggregates by way of the root-condition.
A state consisting of non-initial application and sustained application is a condition, by way of root-condition, for a state without initial application and sustained application:

roots consisting of non-initial application and sustained application are a condition, by way of root-condition, for sustained application and for the mind-produced material phenomena. At the moment of rebirth-linking, roots consisting of non-initial application and sustained application are a condition, by way of root-condition, for sustained application and for the kamma-produced material phenomena.

A state consisting of non-initial application and sustained application is a condition, by way of root-condition, for a state consisting of non-initial application and sustained application, and for a state without initial application and sustained application:

roots consisting of non-initial application and sustained application are a condition, by way of root-condition, for the associated aggregates, for sustained application, and for mind-produced matter. At the moment of rebirth-linking, [roots] consisting of non-initial application and sustained application...
Roots associated with [states] are a condition, by way of root-condition, for their associated aggregates, for vicāra, and for the matter produced by karma (kaṭattā-rūpa).
A state without applied thought and without sustained thought is a condition, by way of root-condition, for a state without applied thought and without sustained thought:
roots without applied thought and without sustained thought are a condition, by way of root-condition, for their associated aggregates and for mind-produced matter.

At the moment of rebirth-linking, roots that are without applied thought and without sustained thought are a condition, by way of root-condition, for the associated aggregates and for the matter produced by kamma.
Object...
A state with applied thought and sustained thought is a condition, by way of object-condition, for a state with applied thought and sustained thought:
having given a gift, undertaken virtue, and performed the Uposatha duty, one reviews that; one reviews former well-performed deeds;
having emerged from jhānas with applied thought and sustained thought, having emerged from the Path, and having emerged from the Fruit, one [reviews] the Fruit.
One reviews. Noble ones review defilements that have been abandoned, review defilements that have been suppressed, and know defilements previously practiced.
They insightfully contemplate the aggregates accompanied by applied and sustained thought as impermanent, suffering, and non-self;
they relish them and delight in them; with that as the object, lust arises … and so on … grief arises.
Taking the aggregates accompanied by applied thought and sustained thought as an object, aggregates accompanied by applied thought and sustained thought arise.
A state accompanied by applied thought and sustained thought is a condition, by way of object-condition, for a state without applied thought but with sustained thought:
having given a gift, undertaken virtue, and performed the Uposatha duty, one reviews that; taking that as an object, applied thought [arises].

It arises. One reviews what was previously well-performed; having emerged from jhāna with applied and sustained thought, having emerged from the path, and having emerged from the fruition, one reviews the fruition; thinking about that, applied thought arises.
Noble ones review defilements abandoned, review defilements suppressed, and [review] what was formerly practiced.

They know the defilements. They practice insight into the aggregates accompanied by initial application and sustained application as impermanent, suffering, and non-self, and they relish and delight in them;
with that as object, initial application arises. Initial application arises taking the aggregates accompanied by initial application and sustained application as its object.

A state accompanied by initial application and sustained application is a condition, by way of object-condition, for a state without initial application and sustained application—by means of the knowledge of penetration into others' minds (*cetopariya-ñāṇa*).

One knows the consciousness of one possessed of consciousness accompanied by applied thought and sustained thought. Aggregates accompanied by applied thought and sustained thought are related to the knowledge of penetration into others' minds, the knowledge of recollection of past lives, the knowledge of the passing away and rebirth of beings according to their deeds, and the knowledge of future existences, by way of object-condition.
Taking aggregates accompanied by applied thought and sustained thought as an object, aggregates without applied thought and sustained thought arise.

A state with applied thought and sustained thought is a condition, by way of object-condition, for a state with applied thought and sustained thought and for a state without applied thought but with sustained thought:
having given a gift, undertaken virtue, and performed the Uposatha duty, one reviews it;
taking that as object, aggregates with applied thought and sustained thought and applied thought itself arise. Previously...

One reviews wholesome deeds well-performed; having emerged from jhānas accompanied by applied and sustained thought, having emerged from the path, and having emerged from the fruit, one reviews the fruit; with that as the object, aggregates accompanied by applied and sustained thought, as well as applied thought itself, arise.
Noble ones review defilements abandoned, and they review defilements suppressed.
They know the defilements previously practiced. They practice insight into the aggregates accompanied by initial and sustained application as impermanent, suffering, and non-self;
they relish them and delight in them; with that as an object, the aggregates accompanied by initial and sustained application and initial application arise.
With the aggregates accompanied by initial and sustained application as an object, the aggregates accompanied by initial and sustained application and initial application arise.
A state consisting of non-initial application and sustained application is a condition for a state consisting of non-initial application and sustained application by way of object-condition:
having emerged from jhānas consisting of non-initial application and sustained application, having emerged from the Path, or having emerged from the Fruit, one reviews the Fruit;

taking that as object, initial application arises. [One contemplates] the aggregates consisting of non-initial application and sustained application, together with initial application, as impermanent, as suffering...
One contemplates [them] as non-self, relishes them, and delights in them; with that as object, thought (vitakka) arises.
With the aggregates that are without thought but have examination (avitakkavicāramatta) and with thought itself as object, thought arises.

A state without thought but with examination is a condition for a state with both thought and examination by way of the object-condition (ārammaṇapaccaya)—[namely,] those states without thought but with examination...
Having emerged from jhāna, having emerged from the path, and having emerged from the fruit, they review the fruit;

conditioned by that, aggregates accompanied by applied thought and sustained thought arise. One contemplates those aggregates—devoid of applied thought but possessing sustained thought—and applied thought itself as impermanent, suffering, and non-self; one relishes them and delights in them; conditioned by that, lust arises.

... pe ... mental distress arises. Taking the aggregates that are without applied thought but with sustained thought (*avitakkavicāramatta*) and applied thought (*vitakka*) as object, aggregates with applied thought and sustained thought (*savitakkasavicāra*) arise.
A state without applied thought but with sustained thought is a condition, by way of object-condition (*ārammaṇapaccaya*), for a state without applied thought and sustained thought:

through the knowledge of penetration of others' minds (*cetopariyañāṇa*), one knows the mind of one possessing a mind without applied thought but with sustained thought. The aggregates without applied thought but with sustained thought [are conditions] for the knowledge of penetration of others' minds.

The knowledge of recollection of past lives, the knowledge of the passing away and reappearance according to karma, and the knowledge of future existences are related [to their respective objects] by way of object-condition (*ārammaṇapaccaya*).

Taking the aggregates accompanied by sustained thought but without applied thought (*avitakkavicāramatta*) and applied thought itself as an object, aggregates that are without both applied and sustained thought (*avitakkavicāra*) arise.

A state accompanied by sustained thought but without applied thought is related to a state with both applied and sustained thought (*savitakkasavicāra*) and to a state accompanied by sustained thought but without applied thought.

Condition by way of object-condition: Having emerged from a jhāna without applied thought but with sustained thought, having emerged from the Path, or having emerged from the Fruit, one reviews the Fruit. Taking that as object, aggregates accompanied by applied and sustained thought, as well as applied thought itself, arise.
[One contemplates] the aggregates and applied thought, which are without applied thought but with sustained thought, as impermanent, as suffering...
One contemplates [the aggregates] as non-self, relishes them, and delights in them;

with that as object, aggregates accompanied by applied thought and sustained thought, as well as applied thought itself, arise. With aggregates that are without applied thought but have sustained thought, and with applied thought itself, as objects, aggregates accompanied by applied thought and sustained thought, as well as applied thought itself, arise.
A state without applied thought and sustained thought is a condition, by way of object-condition, for a state without applied thought and sustained thought:
Nibbāna is a condition, by way of object-condition, for the path without applied thought and sustained thought, for its fruition, and for sustained thought.

By means of the divine eye one sees a visible form; by means of the divine ear-element one hears a sound; by means of the knowledge of penetration into others' minds, [one knows] the mind of one possessing a mind without applied thought and sustained thought...

It knows the mind. The base of infinite space is a condition, by way of object-condition, for the base of infinite consciousness; ... pe ... the base of nothingness is a condition, by way of object-condition, for the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception.
The visible-object base is a condition, by way of object-condition, for eye-consciousness; ... pe ... the tangible-object base is a condition, by way of object-condition, for body-consciousness.
The aggregates without applied thought and sustained thought are conditions, by way of object-condition, for the knowledge of the modes of psychic power and for the knowledge of penetration of minds.

The knowledge of recollection of past lives, the knowledge of passing away according to karma, and the knowledge of future states are related to [their objects] by way of object-condition (*ārammaṇapaccaya*).

Taking the aggregates that are without applied thought and sustained thought (*avitakka-avicāra*) and the sustained thought itself as an object, aggregates that are without applied thought and sustained thought arise.
A state without applied thought and sustained thought is related to a state with applied thought and sustained thought by way of object-condition—the Noble Ones...
Having emerged from jhānas without applied thought and sustained thought, having emerged from the path, and having emerged from the fruit, they review the fruit;

taking that as their object, aggregates with applied thought and sustained thought arise. Noble ones review Nibbāna, [taking] Nibbāna as the object for change-of-lineage, purification, the path with applied thought and sustained thought, the fruit, and adverting.
It is a condition by way of object-condition (*ārammaṇa-paccaya*). One contemplates the eye as impermanent, suffering, and non-self;
one relishes it and delights in it. Taking that as an object, lust arises … [and so on] … grief arises.

[The same applies to] the ear … the nose … the tongue … the body … visible forms … sounds … odors … tastes … tangibles … the physical basis (*vatthu*) … [states] without applied thought and sustained thought (*avitakka-avicāra*).
One contemplates the aggregates and applied thought as impermanent, suffering, and non-self; one relishes them and delights in them.

Taking these as an object, lust arises … [and so on] … grief arises. Taking the aggregates that are without applied thought and sustained thought, as well as sustained thought itself, as an object, the aggregates accompanied by applied thought and sustained thought arise.
A state without applied thought and sustained thought is a condition, by way of object-condition, for a state with applied thought and sustained thought only:
noble ones, having emerged from jhānas without applied thought and sustained thought, having emerged from the path, and having emerged from the fruit, review the fruit;
taking that as an object, applied thought arises. Noble ones review Nibbāna; Nibbāna is [the condition] for a state with applied thought and sustained thought only.
It is a condition for the path, the fruit, and applied thought by way of object-condition.

One contemplates the eye as impermanent, suffering, and non-self … [as before] … the physical basis … and one contemplates the aggregates free from both applied and sustained thought, as well as sustained thought itself, as impermanent, suffering, and non-self;
one relishes them and delights in them. Taking that as an object, applied thought arises. [One contemplates] the aggregates free from both applied and sustained thought … [as before].
And based on examination (*vicāra*), applied thought (*vitakka*) arises.

A state without applied thought and without examination is a condition, by way of object-condition (*ārammaṇapaccaya*), for a state without applied thought and with only examination, and for a state without applied thought and without examination—
namely, Nibbāna is [the condition] for the path, the fruit, and the examination that are without applied thought and with only examination.
And it is a condition by way of object-condition (*ārammaṇapaccaya*).

A state without applied thought and sustained thought (*avitakka-avicāra*) is a condition by way of object-condition for a state with applied thought and sustained thought (*savitakka-savicāra*) and for a state without applied thought but with sustained thought only (*avitakka-vicāramatta*):
namely, when Noble Ones, having emerged from a jhāna without applied thought and sustained thought, or having emerged from the Path, [contemplate it].
Having emerged from fruition, they review the fruition; taking that as their object, aggregates accompanied by applied thought and sustained thought, as well as applied thought itself, arise.

Noble ones review Nibbāna; taking Nibbāna as their object, there arise aggregates accompanied by applied thought and sustained thought, as well as applied thought of change-of-lineage, applied thought of purification, applied thought of the path accompanied by applied thought and sustained thought, and applied thought itself.
The result and the applied thought (vitakka) are related to the adverting consciousness and the applied thought by way of object-condition (ārammaṇapaccaya).

One contemplates the eye as impermanent, suffering, and non-self, and relishes and delights in it; taking that as an object, the aggregates accompanied by applied thought and sustained thought (savitakka-savicāra), as well as the applied thought itself, arise.
[The same applies to] the ear … pe … tangible objects … the physical base … [and] states without applied thought and sustained thought (avitakka-avicāra).
One contemplates the aggregates and applied thought as impermanent, suffering, and non-self; one relishes them and delights in them.
Taking those as an object, aggregates accompanied by applied thought and sustained thought, as well as applied thought itself, arise.

Furthermore, states that are without applied thought but with sustained thought alone, and those that are without both applied thought and sustained thought, [arise] for a state accompanied by applied thought and sustained thought by way of object-condition (*ārammaṇa-paccaya*).

Condition: Taking as object both the aggregates accompanied by sustained thought but devoid of applied thought and the sustained thought itself, the aggregates accompanied by both applied and sustained thought arise.

States devoid of applied thought but accompanied by sustained thought and states devoid of both applied and sustained thought are conditions, by way of object-condition, for states devoid of applied thought but accompanied by sustained thought: taking as object both the aggregates accompanied by sustained thought but devoid of applied thought and the sustained thought itself, applied thought arises.

States devoid of applied thought but accompanied by sustained thought and states devoid of both applied and sustained thought are conditions, by way of object-condition, for a state devoid of both applied and sustained thought.

Condition: Aggregates accompanied by sustained thought but without applied thought, together with sustained thought itself, are related to knowledge of the minds of others, knowledge of recollection of past lives, knowledge of the passing away and rebirth of beings according to their deeds, and knowledge of future existences, by way of object condition.
Taking aggregates accompanied by sustained thought but without applied thought, together with sustained thought itself, as object, aggregates without applied thought or sustained thought arise.
States that are without applied thought but with sustained thought, and states that are without both applied and sustained thought,
are related to states that are with both applied and sustained thought and without applied thought but with sustained thought by way of object condition:
taking the aggregates without applied thought but with sustained thought and sustained thought as object, aggregates with both applied and sustained thought and applied thought arise.

States with applied thought and sustained thought, and states without applied thought but with sustained thought, are related to a state with applied thought and sustained thought by way of object condition:
taking the aggregates with applied thought and sustained thought, as well as applied thought itself, as an object, aggregates with applied thought and sustained thought arise.

States with applied thought and sustained thought, and states without applied thought but with sustained thought, are related to a state without applied thought but with sustained thought by way of object condition: taking the aggregates with applied thought and sustained thought, as well as applied thought itself, as an object, applied thought arises.

States with applied thought and sustained thought, and states without applied thought but with sustained thought, are related to a state without applied thought and sustained thought by way of object condition:

aggregates with applied thought and sustained thought, together with applied thought itself, are related to the knowledge of penetration into others' minds, the knowledge of recollection of past lives, the knowledge of the passing away and rebirth of beings according to their deeds, and the knowledge of future existences, by way of object condition. [In the case of] states with applied thought and sustained thought...
Taking the aggregates and applied thought as object, non-applied and non-sustained aggregates arise. States with applied thought and sustained thought,
and states without applied thought but with sustained thought, are related to states with applied thought and sustained thought,
and states without applied thought but with sustained thought, by way of object condition— taking the aggregates with applied thought and sustained thought, and applied thought, as object.
The aggregates accompanied by applied thought and sustained thought, as well as applied thought itself, arise.
Dominance:

A state accompanied by applied thought and sustained thought is a condition, by way of the dominance condition, for a state accompanied by applied thought and sustained thought—namely, object-dominance.

Conascence-predominance. Object-predominance: having given a gift, undertaken virtue, or performed an observance-day duty, one esteems and reviews it; one esteems and reviews former well-performed deeds.
Having emerged from jhānas accompanied by applied and sustained thought, having emerged from the path, or having emerged from the fruit, one esteems and reviews the fruit.
Taking the aggregates accompanied by applied thought and sustained thought as an object, one esteems them and delights in them;

esteeming them, lust arises and wrong view arises. As co-nascent predominance: a predominance accompanied by applied thought and sustained thought is a condition, by way of predominance condition, for the associated aggregates.

A state with applied thought and sustained thought (*savitakkasavicāra*) is a condition for a state without applied thought but with sustained thought (*avitakkavicāramatta*) by way of predominance condition (*adhipatipaccaya*):

as object-predominance (*ārammaṇādhipati*) and as conascence-predominance (*sahajātādhipati*). As object-predominance: having given a gift, undertaken virtue, or performed the Uposatha duty, one esteems and reviews it;
esteeming it, applied thought arises. [One esteems] past deeds well-performed...

One esteems and reviews it. Having emerged from jhānas with applied thought and sustained thought, having emerged from the path, and having emerged from the fruit, one esteems and reviews the fruit; esteeming that, applied thought arises.
Esteeming and delighting in the aggregates with applied thought and sustained thought, esteeming that, applied thought [arises].

It arises. Conascence-predominance: a predominance accompanied by applied thought and sustained thought (*savitakkasavicārā adhipati*) is a condition for applied thought by way of the predominance-condition (*adhipatipaccaya*).

A state accompanied by applied thought and sustained thought is a condition for a state without applied thought and sustained thought by way of the predominance-condition. Conascence-predominance: a predominance accompanied by applied thought and sustained thought is a condition for mind-produced matter (*cittasamuṭṭhānānaṁ rūpānaṁ*) by way of the predominance-condition.

A state accompanied by applied thought and sustained thought is [a condition] for both states accompanied by applied thought and sustained thought and states without applied thought and sustained thought...

Conditioned by way of predominance condition (*adhipatipaccaya*). Co-nascent predominance (*sahajātādhipati*): a predominance accompanied by applied thought and sustained thought (*savitakkasavicāra*) is a condition by way of predominance condition for its associated aggregates (*khandha*) and for mind-produced matter (*cittasamuṭṭhāna-rūpa*).

A state accompanied by applied thought and sustained thought is [a condition] for a state without applied thought but with sustained thought (*avitakkavicāramatta*), and for a state without applied thought and sustained thought (*avitakka-avicāra*).

Conditioned by way of predominance condition (*adhipatipaccaya*). Co-nascent predominance: a predominance accompanied by applied thought and sustained thought (*savitakkasavicāra*) is a condition by way of predominance for applied thought and for mind-produced matter.

A state accompanied by applied thought and sustained thought is [a condition] for a state accompanied by applied thought and sustained thought and for a state without applied thought but with sustained thought alone.
Condition by way of predominance-condition: objective-predominance and conascence-predominance. Objective-predominance:
having given a gift, undertaken virtue, or performed the Uposatha duty, one esteems it and reviews it;
esteeming it, aggregates accompanied by applied thought and sustained thought, as well as applied thought itself, arise. [One esteems] previously well-performed deeds...
Having emerged from jhānas accompanied by applied thought and sustained thought, having emerged from the path, and having emerged from the fruit, one esteems and reviews the fruit;
esteeming it, aggregates accompanied by applied thought and sustained thought, as well as applied thought itself, arise.
Esteeming the aggregates accompanied by applied thought and sustained thought, one relishes and delights in them.

Making that [condition] predominant, the aggregates accompanied by applied thought and sustained thought (*savitakkasavicāra*), as well as applied thought itself, arise. Co-nascent predominance (*sahajātādhipati*):
a predominance accompanied by applied thought and sustained thought is a condition, by way of predominance-condition (*adhipatipaccaya*), for the associated aggregates and for applied thought.

A state accompanied by applied thought and sustained thought is [a condition] for a state accompanied by applied thought and sustained thought, for a state without applied thought but with sustained thought alone (*avitakkavicāramatta*), and for a state without applied thought and sustained thought (*avitakka-avicāra*).
And [this] is a condition for the state by way of predominance-condition (*adhipatipaccaya*). Co-nascent predominance (*sahajātādhipati*):

a predominance accompanied by applied thought and sustained thought (*savitakkasavicārā*) is a condition by way of predominance-condition for its associated aggregates (*khandha*), for applied thought, and for mind-produced matter (*cittasamuṭṭhāna-rūpa*).

A state consisting of sustained thought without applied thought (*avitakkavicāramatta*) is a condition for a state consisting of sustained thought without applied thought by way of predominance-condition—as object-predominance (*ārammaṇādhipati*).

Conascence-predominance. Object-predominance: having emerged from a jhāna without applied thought but with sustained thought, having emerged from the Path, or having emerged from the Fruit, one esteems and reviews the Fruit; esteeming it, applied thought arises.

Esteeming, enjoying, and delighting in both the aggregates without applied thought but with sustained thought and the applied thought itself, one esteems them... [esteeming them]... [the Fruit arises].
Having performed [the preliminary work], applied thought arises. Co-nascent predominance:

predominance consisting of states without applied thought but with sustained thought is a condition, by way of predominance-condition, for the associated aggregates. A state without applied thought but with sustained thought is a condition, by way of predominance-condition, for a state with both applied and sustained thought.

Object-predominance: Having emerged from a jhāna without applied thought but with sustained thought, having emerged from the path, or having emerged from the fruition, one esteems and reviews the fruition;
esteeming it, aggregates accompanied by applied and sustained thought arise.
Esteeming, relishing, and delighting in both the aggregates without applied thought but with sustained thought and the applied thought itself, one esteems it... [and so on].
Having performed [an action], lust arises; wrong view arises.
A state accompanied by sustained thought but lacking applied thought is a condition, by way of predominance condition, for a state that is without both applied and sustained thought.
Co-nascent predominance: a predominance accompanied by sustained thought but lacking applied thought is a condition for sustained thought and for mind-produced matter.
Conditioned by way of predominance condition (*adhipatipaccaya*).

A state consisting of neither initial application nor sustained application (*avitakkavicāramatta*) is a condition, by way of predominance condition, for a state consisting of neither initial application nor sustained application and for a state without initial application and sustained application.
Conascent predominance (*sahajātādhipati*): a predominance consisting of neither initial application nor sustained application [is a condition] for its associated states...
The aggregates, applied thought, and mind-produced matter are related to [their respective] states by way of predominance condition (*adhipatipaccaya*).

A state consisting of applied thought and sustained thought (*avitakkavicāramatta*) is related to a state with both applied and sustained thought (*savitakkasavicāra*) and to a state consisting of applied thought and sustained thought by way of predominance condition.
Object-predominance (*ārammaṇādhipati*): having emerged from jhānas consisting of applied thought and sustained thought...
Having emerged from the path, having emerged from the fruit, one esteems and reviews the fruit;

esteeming that, aggregates accompanied by applied thought and sustained thought, as well as applied thought itself, arise. Esteeming and delighting in the aggregates accompanied by sustained thought but without applied thought, as well as applied thought itself, esteeming that, [there arise] aggregates accompanied by applied thought and sustained thought...
The aggregates and applied thought arise together.
A state without applied thought and sustained thought is a condition, by way of predominance condition, for a state without applied thought and sustained thought:
as object-predominance and co-nascent predominance. Object-predominance: Nibbāna is a condition for the path without applied thought and sustained thought, for its fruit, and for sustained thought.

And it is a condition by way of predominance-condition (*adhipatipaccaya*). Co-nascent predominance: a predominance without applied thought and sustained thought is a condition by way of predominance-condition for its associated aggregates and for mind-produced matter.
A state without applied thought and sustained thought is a condition by way of predominance-condition for a state with applied thought and sustained thought.

Object-predominance: Noble ones, having emerged from jhānas without applied thought and sustained thought, having emerged from the path, and having emerged from the fruit, esteem and review the fruit; esteeming it, aggregates with applied thought and sustained thought arise.
Noble ones esteem and review Nibbāna; Nibbāna [is related] to change-of-lineage...
It is a condition for purification, for the path with applied thought and sustained thought, and for the fruit, by way of predominance-condition.
Taking the eye as venerable, one relishes it and delights in it; taking it as venerable, lust arises, and wrong view arises.
[The same applies to] the ear … the nose … the tongue … the body … visible forms … sounds … odors … tastes … tangibles … the physical base (vatthu).
... one esteems, relishes, and delights in the aggregates that are without applied thought and sustained thought, as well as sustained thought itself;
by esteeming them, lust arises and wrong view arises.
A state without applied thought and sustained thought is a condition for a state without applied thought but with sustained thought by way of the predominance condition (*adhipatipaccaya*).

Object-predominance: Noble ones, having emerged from jhānas without applied thought and sustained thought, having emerged from the path, and having emerged from the fruit, esteem and review the fruit; esteeming it, applied thought arises.
Noble ones esteem and review Nibbāna; [Nibbāna is the object-predominance] for the path without applied thought and with only sustained thought.
The fruit and the applied thought (*vitakka*) are related by way of the predominance condition (*adhipatipaccaya*). The eye ... [as before] ... the physical basis (*vatthu*) ...

one esteems and delights in the aggregates (*khandha*) that are without applied thought or sustained thought (*avitakkavicāramatta*) and the sustained thought itself; esteeming them, applied thought arises.
A state without applied thought or sustained thought is related to a state without applied thought or sustained thought, and to a state without applied thought but with sustained thought alone.

It is a condition by way of predominance-condition (*adhipatipaccaya*). Object-predominance (*ārammaṇādhipati*): Nibbāna is a condition by way of predominance-condition for the path, the fruit, and sustained thought (*vicāra*) that are without applied thought but with sustained thought (*avitakkavicāramatta*).

A state without applied thought and without sustained thought (*avitakka-avicāra*) is [a condition] for a state with applied thought and sustained thought (*savitakkasavicāra*) and for a state without applied thought but with sustained thought.

It is a condition by way of predominance condition (*adhipatipaccaya*). As object-predominance (*ārammaṇādhipati*): Noble ones, having emerged from jhānas without applied thought and sustained thought, having emerged from the path, and having emerged from the fruit, esteem and review the fruit;
esteeming it, aggregates accompanied by applied and sustained thought and applied thought itself arise. Noble ones esteem Nibbāna...

They review [them]. Nibbāna is related to the change-of-lineage thought, the purification thought, the path with applied thought and sustained thought, and the fruition with applied thought and sustained thought, by way of predominance condition.
Having treated the eye as venerable … [and so on] … the physical basis … [they review] the aggregates without applied thought and sustained thought, and sustained thought.
Valuing it, one relishes and delights in it; valuing that, aggregates accompanied by both initial and sustained application (*savitakka-savicāra*) and initial application (*vitakka*) arise.

States consisting of sustained application only (*avitakka-vicāramatta*) and states without both initial and sustained application (*avitakka-avicāra*) are related to a state accompanied by both initial and sustained application by way of the predominance condition (*adhipatipaccaya*).

As object-predominance (*ārammaṇādhipati*): valuing the aggregates consisting of sustained application only and sustained application itself, aggregates accompanied by both initial and sustained application arise.

States that are either with applied thought and sustained thought only, or without applied thought and sustained thought, are related to a state with applied thought and sustained thought only by way of predominance condition (*adhipatipaccaya*).

As object-predominance (*ārammaṇādhipati*): having taken the aggregates with applied thought and sustained thought only, as well as sustained thought itself, as estimable objects, applied thought arises.

States that are without applied thought but with sustained thought, and states that are without both applied and sustained thought, are related to states with both applied and sustained thought and without applied thought but with sustained thought by way of predominance condition (*adhipatipaccaya*). As object-predominance (*ārammaṇādhipati*):

taking the aggregates without applied thought but with sustained thought and sustained thought itself as an object of esteem, aggregates with both applied and sustained thought and applied thought arise.

States with applied thought and sustained thought (savitakkasavicāra) and states without applied thought but with sustained thought only (avitakkavicāramatta) are related to a state with applied thought and sustained thought by way of predominance condition (adhipatipaccaya). As object-predominance (ārammaṇādhipati):
taking as an object and esteeming the aggregates with applied thought and sustained thought together with applied thought, aggregates with applied thought and sustained thought arise.

States with applied thought and sustained thought, and states without applied thought but with sustained thought, are related to a state without applied thought but with sustained thought by way of predominance condition (*adhipatipaccaya*).
As object-predominance (*ārammaṇādhipati*): having honored both the aggregates with applied thought and sustained thought and the applied thought itself, applied thought arises.

States with applied thought and sustained thought, and states without applied thought but with sustained thought, are related to states with applied thought and sustained thought, and states without applied thought but with sustained thought, by way of predominance condition (*adhipatipaccaya*). As object-predominance (*ārammaṇādhipati*):

having taken the aggregates with applied thought and sustained thought, together with applied thought, as estimable objects (*garuṃ katvā*), the aggregates with applied thought and sustained thought, together with applied thought, arise.
Immediately preceding state with applied thought and sustained thought is related to a subsequent state with applied thought and sustained thought by way of immediate condition:
preceding aggregates with applied thought and sustained thought are related to subsequent aggregates with applied thought and sustained thought.
It is a condition by way of proximity-condition (*anantara-paccaya*). Adaptation (*anuloma*) is a condition for change-of-lineage (*gotrabhū*); adaptation is a condition for purification (*vodāna*);

change-of-lineage is a condition for the path with applied thought and sustained thought (*savitakka-savicāra*); purification is a condition for the path with applied thought and sustained thought; the path with applied thought and sustained thought is a condition for the fruit with applied thought and sustained thought;

the fruit with applied thought and sustained thought is a condition for the fruit with applied thought and sustained thought; adaptation is a condition for [the path] with applied thought and sustained thought...
It is a condition for the attainment of fruition by way of proximity-condition (*anantara-paccaya*).

A state with applied thought and sustained thought (*savitakka-savicāra*) is a condition for a state without applied thought but with sustained thought (*avitakka-vicāramatta*) by way of proximity-condition:
preceding aggregates with applied thought and sustained thought are a condition for succeeding applied thoughts by way of proximity-condition.

Condition. A death-consciousness accompanied by initial application and sustained application is a condition for a rebirth-consciousness without initial application but with sustained application; ... pe ...

aggregates accompanied by initial application and sustained application are a condition for emergence without initial application but with sustained application and for initial application; ... pe ... preparation for absorption without initial application but with sustained application is a condition for absorption without initial application but with sustained application;
... the change-of-lineage is a condition for [absorption] without initial application but with sustained application.
The purification of the path is related to the path that is without applied thought but with sustained thought;
conformity is related to the attainment of fruition that is without applied thought but with sustained thought, and to applied thought, by way of proximity-condition.

A state with applied thought and sustained thought is related to a state without applied thought and sustained thought by way of proximity-condition—the [state] with applied thought and sustained thought...
Life-continuum consciousness is a condition for the rebirth-linking consciousness that is without applied thought and sustained thought, and for sustained thought, by way of proximity condition.

Advertence is a condition for the five types of sense-consciousness by way of proximity condition. Aggregates with applied thought and sustained thought are a condition for emergence without applied thought and sustained thought, and for sustained thought …pe… the preparation for the second jhāna is a condition for sustained thought in the second jhāna.
It is a condition by way of proximity-condition (*anantara-paccaya*).

The preparation for the third jhāna …pe… the preparation for the fourth jhāna …pe… the preparation for the base of infinite space …pe… the preparation for the base of infinite consciousness …pe… the preparation for the base of nothingness …pe… the preparation for the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception …pe…

The preliminary work for the divine eye … the preliminary work for the divine ear-element … the preliminary work for the knowledge of the modes of supernormal power … the preliminary work for the knowledge of penetration of minds … the preliminary work for the knowledge of recollection of past lives … the preliminary work for the knowledge of the passing away and rebirth of beings according to their kamma … the preliminary work for the knowledge of the future … the change-of-lineage.

The purification of the path without applied thought and sustained thought, as well as sustained thought, is related to the path without applied thought and sustained thought, as well as sustained thought;
conformity to the attainment of fruition without applied thought and sustained thought, as well as sustained thought, is related by way of proximity-condition.
A state with applied thought and sustained thought is related to a state without applied thought but with sustained thought, and to a state without applied thought and sustained thought...

Condition by way of proximity condition: a death-consciousness accompanied by applied thought and sustained thought (*savitakka-savicāra*) is a condition by way of proximity condition for a rebirth-consciousness consisting of sustained thought only (*avitakka-vicāramatta*) and for [the mental] sustained thought (*vicāra*).

Aggregates accompanied by applied thought and sustained thought are a condition by way of proximity condition for emergence (*vuṭṭhāna*) consisting of sustained thought only and for [the mental] sustained thought. [This applies to] absorption (*jhāna*) consisting of sustained thought only.

The preliminary stage (*parikamma*) is a condition for the jhāna that is without applied thought but with sustained thought (*avitakkavicāramatta*), and for sustained thought itself, by way of the proximity-condition (*anantarapaccaya*).

The change-of-lineage (*gotrabhu*) is a condition for the path that is without applied thought but with sustained thought, and for sustained thought itself; purification (*vodāna*) is a condition for the path that is without applied thought but with sustained thought, and for sustained thought itself;
conformity (*anuloma*) is a condition for the attainment of fruition that is without applied thought but with sustained thought, and for sustained thought itself.
And it is a condition by way of proximity-condition (*anantara-paccaya*).

A state with applied thought and sustained thought (*savitakka-savicāra*) is a condition for a state with applied thought and sustained thought and for a state without applied thought but with sustained thought alone (*avitakka-vicāramatta*) by way of proximity-condition:
preceding aggregates with applied thought and sustained thought are [conditions] for succeeding [aggregates] with applied thought and sustained thought...
Aggregates accompanied by initial application and sustained application are related to initial application by way of proximity condition.

Adaptation is related to change-of-lineage and initial application … adaptation is related to purification and initial application … change-of-lineage is related to the path accompanied by initial application and sustained application and initial application … purification is related to the path accompanied by initial application and sustained application and initial application … [and] that which is accompanied by initial application and sustained application...

The path is a related condition, by way of proximity-condition, for the fruit with applied thought and sustained thought, for [its] applied thought, and for the fruit with applied thought and sustained thought, for [its] applied thought and sustained thought;

likewise, adaptation is a related condition, by way of proximity-condition, for the attainment of fruition with applied thought and sustained thought, for [its] applied thought, and for [its] applied thought and sustained thought.

A state consisting of non-initial application and sustained application is a condition for a state consisting of non-initial application and sustained application by way of proximity-condition (*anantara-paccaya*).
Each preceding initial application is a condition for each succeeding initial application by way of proximity-condition.

Each preceding aggregate consisting of non-initial application and sustained application is [a condition] for each succeeding aggregate consisting of non-initial application and sustained application...

[It is] a condition for the aggregates by way of proximity-condition (*anantara-paccaya*). A path consisting of non-initial application and sustained application (*avitakka-vicāramatta*) is a condition for a fruit consisting of non-initial application and sustained application;
a fruit consisting of non-initial application and sustained application is a condition for a fruit consisting of non-initial application and sustained application by way of proximity-condition.

A state consisting of non-initial application and sustained application is a condition for a state with initial application and sustained application (*savitakka-savicāra*) by way of proximity-condition—the preceding...

The preceding applied thought (*vitakka*) is a condition for each of the subsequent aggregates accompanied by both applied and sustained thought (*savitakkasavicāra*) by way of proximity-condition (*anantara-paccaya*).

The death-consciousness (*cuti-citta*) consisting of sustained thought only without applied thought is a condition for the rebirth-consciousness (*upapatti-citta*) accompanied by both applied and sustained thought by way of proximity-condition.

The life-continuum (*bhavaṅga*) consisting of sustained thought only without applied thought is a condition for adverting (*āvajjanā*) by way of proximity-condition. [The consciousness] consisting of sustained thought only without applied thought...
The aggregates are related to emergence accompanied by applied thought and sustained thought by way of proximity condition.
A state without applied thought but with sustained thought is related to a state without applied thought and sustained thought by way of proximity condition—
the preceding aggregates without applied thought but with sustained thought are related to the succeeding sustained thought by way of proximity condition.

Condition: A death-consciousness accompanied by sustained thought but lacking applied thought, as well as applied thought itself, is a condition by way of proximity-condition for a rebirth-consciousness that is without both applied and sustained thought, and for sustained thought.

Aggregates accompanied by sustained thought but lacking applied thought, as well as applied thought itself, are a condition by way of proximity-condition for emergence that is without both applied and sustained thought, and for sustained thought.

A state consisting of non-initial application and sustained application is a condition, by way of proximity-condition, for a state consisting of non-initial application and sustained application, and for a state consisting of neither initial application nor sustained application:

preceding aggregates consisting of non-initial application and sustained application are a condition, by way of proximity-condition, for subsequent aggregates consisting of non-initial application and sustained application, and for sustained application. A state consisting of non-initial application and sustained application...

The path is related to the fruit that consists of non-initial application and sustained application only, and to sustained application, by way of proximity condition. The fruit that consists of non-initial application and sustained application only is related to the fruit that consists of non-initial application and sustained application only, and to sustained application, by way of proximity condition.

A state consisting of non-initial application and sustained application only is related to a state with both initial and sustained application, and to a state consisting of non-initial application and sustained application only... [by way of proximity condition].

Condition by way of proximity condition: each preceding applied thought (*vitakka*) is a condition, by way of proximity condition, for each subsequent aggregate accompanied by applied thought and sustained thought (*savitakkasavicāra*), as well as for the applied thought itself.

A death-consciousness (*cuticitta*) consisting of sustained thought only (*avitakkavicāramatta*) is a condition, by way of proximity condition, for a rebirth-consciousness (*upapatticitta*) accompanied by applied thought and sustained thought, as well as for the applied thought itself. [A death-consciousness] consisting of sustained thought only...
The life-continuum (bhavaṅga) is related to advertence (āvajjanā) and initial application (vitakka) by way of proximity condition (anantara-paccaya).

Aggregates without initial application but with sustained application (avitakkavicāramattā khandhā) are related to emergence accompanied by both initial and sustained application (savitakkasavicāra vuṭṭhāna) and to initial application by way of proximity condition.

A state without initial application and without sustained application (avitakkaavicāro dhammo) is related to a state without initial application and without sustained application by way of proximity condition—the preceding...
The preceding sustained thought (*vicāra*) is a condition for each subsequent sustained thought by way of proximity-condition (*anantara-paccaya*).

Preceding aggregates (*khandha*) without applied thought (*avitakka*) and sustained thought (*avicāra*) are conditions for subsequent aggregates without applied thought and sustained thought by way of proximity-condition.
A path without applied thought and sustained thought is a condition for a fruit without applied thought and sustained thought... [a state] without applied thought and sustained thought...

The fruit [of absorption] is a condition for the fruit of absorption that is without applied thought and sustained thought by way of proximity condition. For one emerging from cessation, the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception is a condition for the sustained thought of the fruit-attainment that is without applied thought and sustained thought by way of proximity condition.

A state without applied thought and sustained thought is a condition for a state with applied thought and sustained thought by way of proximity condition—the state without applied thought and sustained thought...

Initial application (*vitakka*) and sustained application (*vicāra*) are related to the consciousness of rebirth (*upapatti-citta*) accompanied by both initial and sustained application by way of proximity condition (*anantara-paccaya*).
The life-continuum (*bhavaṅga*) without initial or sustained application and sustained application are related to adverting (*āvajjana*) by way of proximity condition.

The aggregates without initial or sustained application and sustained application are related to emergence (*vuṭṭhāna*) accompanied by both initial and sustained application by way of proximity condition. [From] cessation...

For one emerging from the attainment of the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception, that attainment is a condition for the fruition-attainment accompanied by applied thought and sustained thought by way of proximity-condition.
A state without applied thought and sustained thought is a condition for a state without applied thought but with sustained thought by way of proximity-condition:
each preceding sustained thought is a condition for each subsequent aggregate without applied thought but with sustained thought by way of proximity-condition.

Condition: A death-consciousness without applied thought and sustained thought, as well as sustained thought, is a condition by way of proximity-condition for a rebirth-consciousness accompanied by applied thought but without sustained thought, and for applied thought.

Aggregates without applied thought and sustained thought, as well as sustained thought, are a condition by way of proximity-condition for emergence accompanied by applied thought but without sustained thought, and for applied thought.
For one emerging from cessation, the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception...

A state without applied thought but with sustained thought is related to the attainment of fruition that is without applied thought but with sustained thought, and to a state without applied thought and without sustained thought, by way of proximity condition.
Each preceding instance of sustained thought is related to each succeeding instance of a state without applied thought but with sustained thought by way of proximity condition.

The aggregates are related to investigation by way of proximity-condition (*anantara-paccaya*). A death-consciousness without applied thought and sustained thought is related to a rebirth-consciousness with non-applied and sustained-only thought, and to investigation, by way of proximity-condition.
Aggregates without applied thought and sustained thought are related to emergence with non-applied and sustained-only thought, and to investigation, by way of proximity-condition. From cessation...

For one emerging from the attainment of fruition that is without applied thought and with mere sustained thought (avitakkavicāramatta), the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception (nevasaññānāsaññāyatana) is a condition for that sustained thought by way of proximity-condition (anantarapaccaya).

A state without applied thought and without sustained thought (avitakka-avicāra) is a condition for a state with applied thought and sustained thought (savitakka-savicāra) and for a state without applied thought and with mere sustained thought (avitakkavicāramatta).

Condition by way of proximity condition: a death-consciousness without applied thought and sustained thought, as well as sustained thought, is a condition by way of proximity condition for the rebirth-consciousness with applied thought and sustained thought, and for applied thought.

The life-continuum without applied thought and sustained thought, as well as sustained thought, is a condition by way of proximity condition for adverting and for applied thought. The aggregates without applied thought and sustained thought...
Investigation is a condition, by way of proximity-condition, for emergence accompanied by applied thought and sustained thought,

and for applied thought. For one emerging from cessation, the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception is a condition, by way of proximity-condition, for the attainment of fruition accompanied by applied thought and sustained thought, and for applied thought.

States consisting of neither initial application nor sustained application, and states without initial application and sustained application, are related to a state with both initial application and sustained application by way of proximity condition.

The death-consciousness consisting of neither initial application nor sustained application and sustained application are related to the rebirth-consciousness with both initial application and sustained application by way of proximity condition.
The life-continuum consisting of neither initial application nor sustained application and sustained application are related to adverting [consciousness]... [by way of proximity condition].

It is a condition by way of proximity-condition (*anantara-paccaya*). Aggregates accompanied by sustained thought but devoid of applied thought (*avitakka-vicāramatta*) and sustained thought itself are conditions by way of proximity-condition for emergence accompanied by both applied and sustained thought (*savitakka-savicāra*).

Furthermore, states that are either accompanied by sustained thought but devoid of applied thought, or devoid of both applied and sustained thought, are conditions for a state accompanied by sustained thought but devoid of applied thought.

Condition by way of proximity condition: preceding aggregates accompanied by sustained thought but without applied thought, together with sustained thought, are a condition for subsequent aggregates accompanied by sustained thought but without applied thought by way of proximity condition.

Also, the path accompanied by sustained thought but without applied thought, together with sustained thought, is a condition for the fruit accompanied by sustained thought but without applied thought by way of proximity condition.

Condition: The fruit that is without applied thought but with sustained thought, and sustained thought itself, are conditions by way of proximity-condition for the fruit that is without applied thought but with sustained thought.

States that are without applied thought but with sustained thought, and states that are without applied thought and without sustained thought, are conditions by way of proximity-condition for a state that is without applied thought and without sustained thought.

Condition: Preceding aggregates accompanied by sustained thought but without applied thought, together with sustained thought, are related to succeeding sustained thoughts by way of proximity condition (*anantara-paccaya*).

Death-consciousness accompanied by sustained thought but without applied thought, together with sustained thought, is related to rebirth-consciousness without applied thought or sustained thought by way of proximity condition. [Aggregates] accompanied by sustained thought but without applied thought...
The aggregates and sustained thought are related to emergence that is without applied thought and sustained thought by way of proximity-condition.

States consisting of applied thought and sustained thought, and states without applied thought and sustained thought, are related to states consisting of applied thought and sustained thought, and states without applied thought and sustained thought, by way of proximity-condition—
the preceding aggregates consisting of applied thought and sustained thought [are related to the succeeding ones].

And sustained thought (vicāra) is a condition, by way of proximity-condition, for the subsequent aggregates that are without applied thought but with sustained thought, and for sustained thought itself.

The path that is without applied thought but with sustained thought, together with sustained thought, is a condition, by way of proximity-condition, for the fruit that is without applied thought but with sustained thought, and for sustained thought itself. The fruit that is without applied thought but with sustained thought, and sustained thought...
And [the state] with applied thought and sustained thought only is a condition, by way of proximity-condition, for the fruit with sustained thought only and for sustained thought.
States with applied thought and sustained thought only and states without applied thought and sustained thought are conditions,

by way of proximity-condition, for states with applied thought and sustained thought and for states with sustained thought only— namely, the death-consciousness with sustained thought only and sustained thought.

And the life-continuum accompanied by applied thought and sustained thought, as well as the applied thought itself, are related to the rebirth-consciousness accompanied by applied thought and sustained thought, and to the applied thought, by way of proximity-condition.

The life-continuum without applied thought but with sustained thought, as well as the sustained thought itself, are related to the adverting consciousness and the applied thought by way of proximity-condition.
The aggregates without applied thought but with sustained thought, as well as the sustained thought itself, are related to the emergence accompanied by applied thought and sustained thought...
And it is a condition for thought by way of proximity-condition (*anantara-paccaya*).

States that possess both applied and sustained thought (*savitakka-savicāra*) and states that are without applied thought but possess sustained thought only (*avitakka-vicāramatta*) are conditions for a state possessing both applied and sustained thought by way of proximity-condition—
the preceding aggregates possessing both applied and sustained thought, together with applied thought, [are conditions] for the succeeding [aggregates].
It is a condition for subsequent aggregates with applied thought and sustained thought by way of proximity-condition.
Adaptation and applied thought are conditions for change-of-lineage; adaptation and applied thought are conditions for purification;

change-of-lineage and applied thought are conditions for the path with applied thought and sustained thought; and purification and applied thought are conditions for the path with applied thought and sustained thought.
… both the path with applied thought and sustained thought and the applied thought are related to the fruit with applied thought and sustained thought by way of proximity condition;

both the fruit with applied thought and sustained thought and the applied thought are related to the fruit with applied thought and sustained thought by way of proximity condition; and both adaptation and the applied thought are related to the attainment of the fruit with applied thought and sustained thought by way of proximity condition.

States with applied thought and sustained thought, and states without applied thought but with sustained thought, are related to a state without applied thought but with sustained thought by way of proximity condition:

preceding aggregates with applied thought and sustained thought, together with applied thought itself, are related to succeeding applied thought by way of proximity condition; and the death-consciousness with applied thought and sustained thought...

Initial application (vitakka) is a condition for an arising consciousness that is without initial application but with sustained application (avitakkavicāramatta) by way of proximity-condition (anantarapaccaya).

Aggregates accompanied by both initial and sustained application, as well as initial application itself, are conditions for an emergence (vuṭṭhāna) that is without initial application but with sustained application by way of proximity-condition.

The preliminary work (parikamma) for absorption without initial application but with sustained application, as well as initial application itself, are conditions for absorption without initial application but with sustained application [by way of proximity-condition].

It is a condition by way of proximity-condition (*anantara-paccaya*). Both change-of-lineage and applied thought are a condition by way of proximity-condition for the path that is without applied thought but with sustained thought;

both purification and applied thought are a condition by way of proximity-condition for the path that is without applied thought but with sustained thought; and both conformity and applied thought are a condition by way of proximity-condition for the attainment of fruition that is without applied thought but with sustained thought.

States with applied thought and sustained thought, and states without applied thought but with sustained thought, are related to a state without applied thought and sustained thought by way of proximity condition (*anantara-paccaya*).

The death-consciousness accompanied by applied thought and sustained thought, together with applied thought, is related to the rebirth-consciousness without applied thought and sustained thought, and to sustained thought, by way of proximity condition.
Also, adverting consciousness and applied thought are related to the fivefold sense-consciousnesses...

It is a condition by way of proximity-condition (*anantara-paccaya*). The aggregates accompanied by applied thought and sustained thought (*savitakka-savicāra*), together with applied thought, are a condition by way of proximity-condition for emergence (*vuṭṭhāna*) that is without applied thought and without sustained thought (*avitakka-avicāra*), and for sustained thought.

Furthermore, the preparation (*parikamma*) for the second jhāna and applied thought are a condition by way of proximity-condition for sustained thought in the second jhāna. Also, the preparation for the third jhāna...

Applied thought …pe… both the preparation for the fourth jhāna and applied thought …pe… both the preparation for the base of infinite space and applied thought …pe… both the preparation for the base of infinite consciousness and applied thought …pe… both the preparation for the base of nothingness and applied thought …pe… both the preparation for the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception and applied thought …pe…

The preliminary work for the divine eye and applied thought … pe … the preliminary work for the divine ear-element and applied thought … pe … the preliminary work for the knowledge of the modes of supernormal power and applied thought … pe … the preliminary work for the knowledge of penetration of minds and applied thought … pe … the preliminary work for the knowledge of recollection of past lives and applied thought … pe …

The preparation for the knowledge of the passing away and rebirth of beings according to their kamma and applied thought... [and so on] ...the preparation for the knowledge of future existences and applied thought...
[and so on] ...change-of-lineage and applied thought for the path without applied thought and sustained thought, and for sustained thought...
purification and applied thought for the path without applied thought and sustained thought, and for sustained thought... conformity and applied thought...

And [states] without applied thought and sustained thought are related to the attainment of fruition (phalasamāpatti) without applied thought and sustained thought, and to sustained thought, by way of proximity-condition (anantarapaccaya).
States with applied thought and sustained thought, and states without applied thought but with sustained thought, are related to states without applied thought but with sustained thought,
and to states without applied thought and sustained thought, by way of proximity-condition— the death-consciousness with applied thought and sustained thought, and applied thought.
It is a condition for the rebirth-consciousness accompanied by sustained thought but without applied thought, and for sustained thought itself, by way of proximity-condition (*anantara-paccaya*).

Aggregates accompanied by both applied and sustained thought, as well as applied thought itself, are conditions for the emergence-consciousness accompanied by sustained thought but without applied thought, and for sustained thought itself, by way of proximity-condition.
Furthermore, the preparatory stage (*parikamma*) for absorption accompanied by sustained thought but without applied thought, and applied thought...

And [the state] without applied thought but with sustained thought is a condition for the jhāna without applied thought but with sustained thought and for sustained thought by way of proximity-condition (*anantara-paccaya*).
Change-of-lineage and applied thought are a condition for the path without applied thought but with sustained thought and for sustained thought by way of proximity-condition.
Purification and applied thought are a condition for the path without applied thought but with sustained thought and for sustained thought … and adaptation (*anuloma*) and [applied thought]...

Applied thought (*vitakka*) is a condition for the attainment of fruition that is without applied thought but with sustained thought (*avitakkavicāramatta*), and for sustained thought (*vicāra*), by way of the proximity-condition (*anantarapaccaya*).

Both states that possess both applied and sustained thought (*savitakkasavicāra*) and those that are without applied thought but with sustained thought are conditions for states that possess both applied and sustained thought and those that are without applied thought but with sustained thought, by way of the proximity-condition—the preceding aggregates that possess both applied and sustained thought... [and so on].

Initial application (vitakka) is a condition for each of the subsequent aggregates accompanied by initial and sustained application, and for initial application itself, by way of the proximity condition (anantarapaccaya).

Adaptation (anuloma), adaptation and initial application, are conditions for change-of-lineage (gotrabhū) and initial application; adaptation, adaptation and initial application, are conditions for purification (vodāna) and initial application;
and change-of-lineage and initial application are conditions for [the path] accompanied by initial and sustained application...
And purification and applied thought are related to the path with applied and sustained thought and to applied thought by way of proximity-condition (*anantara-paccaya*).

The path with applied and sustained thought and applied thought are related to the fruit with applied and sustained thought and to applied thought... and the fruit with applied and sustained thought and applied thought... [are related]... by way of proximity-condition.

And [the state] with applied thought and sustained thought is a condition, by way of proximity-condition (*anantara-paccaya*), for the fruit with applied thought and sustained thought, for applied thought itself, and for the conformity [knowledge] (*anuloma*) as well as for applied thought;
it is also a condition, by way of proximity-condition, for the attainment of fruition (*phala-samāpatti*) with applied thought and sustained thought, and for applied thought itself.
Proximity.

A state accompanied by initial application and sustained application is a condition for a state accompanied by initial application and sustained application by way of the proximity condition. (The proximity condition and the contiguity condition are identical.
Co-nascence:

A state accompanied by initial application and sustained application is a condition for a state accompanied by initial application and sustained application by way of the co-nascence condition—a state accompanied by initial application and sustained application...
One aggregate is a condition for three aggregates by way of co-nascence condition; three aggregates are a condition for one aggregate by way of co-nascence condition;
two aggregates are a condition for two aggregates by way of co-nascence condition.

At the moment of rebirth-linking, one aggregate accompanied by applied thought and sustained thought is [a condition] for three aggregates … [and so on] … two aggregates [are a condition for two aggregates].
Of two aggregates ... [etc. ...
