faith, virtue, learning, generosity, and wisdom, as well as applied thought (*vitakka*), which consist of sustained thought without applied thought, are conditions for faith that consists of sustained thought without applied thought … [and so on].
Virtue … learning … generosity … wisdom, and sustained thought are related to [these] by way of decisive support condition (*upanissaya-paccaya*).

A state consisting of non-initial application and sustained thought alone is related to a state with both initial and sustained application, and to a state consisting of non-initial application and sustained thought alone,
by way of decisive support condition— namely, as object-decisive support (*ārammaṇūpanissaya*), proximity-decisive support (*anantarūpanissaya*), and natural-decisive support (*pakatūpanissaya*).
... [as before] ... Natural strong-dependence (*pakatūpanissaya*): faith accompanied by applied thought and sustained thought (*savitakkasavicārā saddhā*), virtue, learning, generosity, and wisdom;

and applied thought (*vitakka*) are related to faith accompanied by applied thought and sustained thought, ... [and so on] ... to aspiration and applied thought, by way of the condition of strong-dependence.

A state without applied thought and without sustained thought (*avitakka-avicāra*) is related to a state without applied thought and without sustained thought by way of the condition of strong-dependence—namely, as object-strong-dependence (*ārammaṇūpanissaya*).
Proximity-predominance condition, natural-predominance condition … [as above] … Natural-predominance condition:

depending on faith that is without applied thought and sustained thought, one arouses jhāna that is without applied thought and sustained thought; one arouses the path … [as above] … superknowledge … [as above] … attainment.
[Depending on] virtue that is without applied thought and sustained thought … learning … generosity … wisdom … sustained thought … bodily pleasure … [one arouses jhāna, etc. … [as above].
… bodily pain … temperature … food … depending on lodgings, one arouses jhāna without applied thought and sustained thought;
one arouses the path … [and so on] … higher knowledge … [and so on] … attainment.
Confidence without applied thought and sustained thought … virtue … learning … generosity … wisdom … sustained thought … bodily pleasure … bodily pain … temperature … [are likewise related].
Food … lodging … is related to confidence free from applied thought and sustained thought, to virtue, to learning, to generosity, to wisdom, to sustained thought,
and to bodily pleasure and bodily pain, by way of decisive support condition (*upanissaya-paccaya*).

A state free from applied thought and sustained thought is related to a state with applied thought and sustained thought by way of decisive support condition— namely, as object-decisive-support (*ārammaṇūpanissaya*).
Proximity-predominance condition, natural-predominance condition … [and so on] … Natural-predominance condition:
depending on faith that is without applied thought and sustained thought, one gives a gift, undertakes precepts, performs the Uposatha duties,
arouses jhāna accompanied by applied and sustained thought, arouses insight … [and so on] … the Path … [and so on] … attainment, or conceives conceit.
One adopts a view. One adopts virtue that is without applied thought and sustained thought; learning ... generosity ... wisdom ...

sustained thought ... bodily pleasure ... bodily pain ... temperature ... food ... or the resting place as a decisive support (upanissaya) for giving a gift, undertaking virtue, performing the Uposatha duty, arousing jhāna accompanied by applied and sustained thought, or [arousing] insight.
... pe ... [one] arouses the path ... pe ... the attainment; one kills a living being ... pe ... one causes a schism in the Saṅgha.

Faith without applied thought and sustained thought (*avitakka-avicārā saddhā*) ... pe ... is related to lodging (*senāsana*), faith with applied thought and sustained thought (*savitakka-savicārā saddhā*), virtue ... pe ... and aspiration, by way of decisive support condition (*upanissaya-paccaya*).

A state without applied thought and sustained thought is related to a state with applied thought but without sustained thought by way of decisive support condition—namely, as object-decisive-support (*ārammaṇūpanissaya*).
Proximity-natural-decisive-support (*anantarūpanissaya*), natural-decisive-support (*pakatūpanissaya*) … [as above] … Natural-decisive-support:

depending on faith that is without applied thought and sustained thought (*avitakka-avicāra*), one arouses jhāna with no applied thought but with sustained thought alone (*avitakkavicāramatta*); one arouses insight … [as above] … the Path … [as above] … attainment.
Depending on virtue that is without applied thought and sustained thought … [as above] … the lodging-place, one arouses jhāna with no applied thought but with sustained thought alone.
It produces insight … [and so on] … it produces the path … [and so on] … it produces attainment.

Confidence without applied thought and sustained thought … [and so on] … the lodging-place is a strong-dependence condition for confidence without applied thought and with only sustained thought, for virtue, for learning, for generosity, for wisdom, and for applied thought.

A state without applied thought and without sustained thought is a condition, by way of decisive support condition (*upanissaya-paccaya*), for a state that has neither applied thought nor sustained thought, and for a state with applied thought and sustained thought only—
namely, as object-decisive support (*ārammaṇūpanissaya*), proximity-decisive support (*anantarūpanissaya*), and natural decisive support (*pakatūpanissaya*) … [as before] … Natural decisive support:
faith without applied thought and without sustained thought … [as before] … the lodging-place [is a condition] for a state with applied thought and sustained thought only.
Faith … virtue … learning … generosity … wisdom, and sustained thought are related to [their respective opposites] by way of decisive support condition (*upanissaya-paccaya*).

A state without applied thought and without sustained thought (*avitakka-avicāra*) is related to a state with applied thought and sustained thought (*savitakka-savicāra*) and to a state without applied thought but with sustained thought only (*avitakka-vicāramatta*) by way of decisive support condition—
namely, as object-decisive support (*ārammaṇūpanissaya*), proximity-decisive support (*anantarūpanissaya*), and natural decisive support (*pakatūpanissaya*).
... [etc] ... Natural decisive support (*pakatūpanissaya*): faith without applied thought and sustained thought (*avitakka-avicārā saddhā*) ... [etc] ...
lodging-place is a condition by way of decisive support for faith with applied thought and sustained thought, for virtue, ... [etc] ... for aspiration and for applied thought.

States that are both without applied thought and with only sustained thought, and those that are without applied thought and without sustained thought, are conditions by way of decisive support for a state with applied thought and sustained thought.
Condition: object-strong-dependence, proximity-strong-dependence, natural strong-dependence ... [etc] ... Natural strong-dependence:
faith without applied thought but with sustained thought, virtue, learning, generosity, and wisdom, as well as sustained thought, are related to faith with both applied and sustained thought ...
[and so on] ... to aspiration by way of the condition of strong-dependence.

States that are without applied thought but with sustained thought, and states that are without applied thought and without sustained thought, are related to a state without applied thought but with sustained thought by way of decisive support condition (upanissaya-paccaya)—namely, object-decisive support, proximity-decisive support, and natural decisive support … [as appropriate] … Natural decisive support:
faith without applied thought but with sustained thought; virtue; learning; generosity; wisdom; and sustained thought.
And faith that is without applied thought but with sustained thought, virtue, learning, generosity, wisdom,
and applied thought are related to [their respective fruits] by way of the decisive support condition (*upanissaya-paccaya*).

Furthermore, states that are without applied thought but with sustained thought, and states that are without applied thought and without sustained thought, are related to a state that is without applied thought and without sustained thought by way of the decisive support condition.
Condition: proximity-strong-dependence (anantarūpanissaya) and natural strong-dependence (pakatūpanissaya) … [as above] … Natural strong-dependence:

faith without applied thought and with sustained thought only; virtue; learning; generosity; wisdom; and sustained thought are conditions for faith without applied thought and without sustained thought, for virtue, for learning, for generosity, for wisdom, and for sustained thought, as well as for bodily pleasure and bodily pain.
Condition by way of decisive support condition (*upanissaya-paccaya*).

States that are without applied thought but with sustained thought (*avitakka-vicāramatta*) and states that are without applied thought and without sustained thought (*avitakka-avicāra*) are related to states that are without applied thought but with sustained thought and states that are without applied thought and without sustained thought by way of decisive support condition—
namely, proximity-decisive support (*anantara-upanissaya*) and natural decisive support (*pakata-upanissaya*) …pe….

Natural strong-dependence: faith without applied thought but with sustained thought; virtue; learning; generosity; wisdom; and sustained thought are related to faith, virtue, learning, generosity, wisdom, and sustained thought—each being without applied thought but with sustained thought—by way of the condition of strong-dependence.

States that are without applied thought but with sustained thought, and states that are without applied thought and without sustained thought, are related to a state with applied thought and sustained thought, and to a state without applied thought but with sustained thought, by way of decisive support condition (upanissaya-paccaya)—namely, object-decisive support, proximity-decisive support, and natural-decisive support … [etc. … Natural-decisive support:
faith without applied thought but with sustained thought; virtue; learning; generosity; wisdom; and sustained thought.
And faith accompanied by applied thought and sustained thought (*savitakka-savicārā saddhā*), virtue (*sīla*), learning (*suta*), generosity (*cāga*), wisdom (*paññā*),

lust (*rāga*), hatred (*dosa*), delusion (*moha*), conceit (*māna*), wrong view (*diṭṭhi*), aspiration (*patthanā*), and applied thought (*vitakka*) are related to [their respective counterparts] by way of decisive support condition (*upanissaya-paccaya*).

States that are both with applied thought and sustained thought, as well as those without applied thought but with sustained thought alone, are related to a state with applied thought and sustained thought...
Condition by way of decisive support condition (upanissaya-paccaya): object-decisive support, proximity-decisive support, natural decisive support … [etc.
… Natural decisive support: confidence accompanied by applied thought and sustained thought; virtue; learning; generosity; wisdom; lust;
hatred; delusion; conceit; wrong view; aspiration; and applied thought are [conditions] for confidence accompanied by applied thought and sustained thought.
Virtue … [and so on] … aspiration is related to [virtue, etc. by way of decisive support condition (*upanissaya-paccaya*).

States that are both with applied thought and sustained thought (*savitakka-savicāra*) and without applied thought but with sustained thought (*avitakka-vicāramatta*) are related to a state without applied thought but with sustained thought by way of decisive support condition:
as object-decisive support (*ārammaṇūpanissaya*), proximity-decisive support (*anantarūpanissaya*), and natural decisive support (*pakatūpanissaya*).

... [etc] ... Natural decisive support (*pakatūpanissaya*): faith accompanied by applied thought and sustained thought (*savitakkasavicārā saddhā*), virtue (*sīla*) ... [etc] ... aspiration (*patthanā*) and applied thought (*vitakka*) are related to faith without applied thought but with sustained thought (*avitakkavicāramattāya saddhāya*), to virtue, to learning (*suta*), to generosity (*cāga*), to wisdom (*paññā*), and to applied thought, by way of the decisive support condition (*upanissayapaccayena paccayo*).

Phenomena that are both accompanied by applied thought and sustained thought, and those that are without applied thought but with sustained thought, are related to a phenomenon without applied thought and sustained thought by way of the decisive support condition.
Condition: proximity-predominance condition, natural-predominance condition …pe…. Natural-predominance condition:

faith accompanied by applied thought and sustained thought; virtue; learning; generosity; wisdom …pe… aspiration and applied thought [are conditions] for faith, virtue, learning, generosity, wisdom, and sustained thought that are without applied thought and without sustained thought, as well as for bodily pleasure.
It is a condition for bodily suffering by way of decisive support condition (*upanissaya-paccaya*).

States that are both with applied thought and sustained thought (*savitakka-savicāra*) and without applied thought but with sustained thought (*avitakka-vicāramatta*) are conditions for states that are without applied thought but with sustained thought and without both applied and sustained thought (*avitakka-avicāra*) by way of decisive support condition—
namely, as proximity-decisive support (*anantara-upanissaya*) and natural decisive support (*pakata-upanissaya*) … [and so forth] …
Natural strong-dependence: faith accompanied by applied thought and sustained thought; virtue; learning; generosity; wisdom; ... pe ...

aspiration and applied thought are related to faith without applied thought but with sustained thought, to virtue, to learning, to generosity, to wisdom, and to sustained thought, by way of the condition of strong-dependence.

States with applied thought and sustained thought, and states without applied thought but with sustained thought only, are related to states with applied thought and sustained thought, and states without applied thought but with sustained thought only, by way of decisive support condition (upanissaya-paccaya)—namely:
object-decisive support, proximity-decisive support, and natural decisive support … [etc. … Natural decisive support:
faith with applied thought and sustained thought … virtue … learning … generosity … wisdom … lust … [and so forth].

… hatred … delusion … conceit … view … and aspiration and applied thought are related to faith with applied thought and sustained thought … pe … to aspiration and to applied thought by way of decisive support condition (*upanissaya-paccaya*).
Pre-arisen (*purejāta*).
A state without applied thought and sustained thought is a condition, by way of prenascence condition, for a state without applied thought and sustained thought:
namely, object-prenascence and base-prenascence. As for object-prenascence: one sees a visible form with the divine eye; one hears a sound with the divine ear-element;
the visible-form base [is a condition] for eye-consciousness ... [and so on] ... the tangible-object base [is a condition] for body-consciousness.

A state without applied thought and sustained thought is a condition for a state with applied thought and sustained thought by way of prenascence condition: namely, as object-prenascence.

The aggregates are related to [other] aggregates by way of the prenascence condition.

A state without applied thought and sustained thought is related to a state without applied thought but with sustained thought by way of the prenascence condition—namely, object-prenascence and base-prenascence.
Object-prenascence: one contemplates the eye as impermanent, suffering, and non-self, and relishes it.
One relishes and delights in it; with that as object, a thought arises. …pe… One practices insight into the basis as impermanent, suffering, and non-self;
one relishes and delights in it; with that as object, a thought arises. Basis-prenascence:
the basis is a condition, by way of prenascence-condition, for the aggregates accompanied by sustained thought but without applied thought, and for applied thought.

A state without applied thought and sustained thought is a condition, by way of prenascence condition, for a state that has no applied thought but has sustained thought, and for a state that has neither applied thought nor sustained thought.

As prenascence of the physical basis (*vatthupurejāta*): the physical basis is a condition, by way of prenascence condition, for the aggregates that have no applied thought but have sustained thought, and for sustained thought.

A state without applied thought and without sustained thought is a condition, by way of prenascence condition, for a state with applied thought and sustained thought, and for a state without applied thought but with sustained thought alone—namely, as object-prenascence and base-prenascence. As object-prenascence:
one contemplates the eye as impermanent, suffering, and non-self; one relishes it and delights in it; taking that as an object, [arise] states with applied thought and sustained thought...

The aggregates and applied thought arise. [One] contemplates the ear … the nose … the tongue … the body … visible forms … sounds … odors … tastes … tangibles … the physical basis as impermanent, suffering, and non-self;

one relishes it and delights in it. Taking that as an object, the aggregates accompanied by applied thought and sustained thought, and applied thought, arise. This is the pre-existence of the physical basis—the physical basis.
Aggregates accompanied by initial application and sustained application, as well as initial application itself, are related to [their concomitants] by way of pre-nascence condition.
Post-nascence:

A state accompanied by initial application and sustained application is related to a state without initial application and sustained application by way of post-nascence condition—the post-nascent aggregates accompanied by initial application and sustained application are related to this pre-nascent body by way of post-nascence condition.
A state consisting of non-thinking and sustained thought is a condition, by way of posterior-nascence condition, for a state without thinking and sustained thought:
the posteriorly arisen aggregates consisting of non-thinking and sustained thought, together with thinking, are a condition, by way of posterior-nascence condition, for this previously arisen body.
A state without thinking and sustained thought is a condition, by way of posterior-nascence condition, for a state without thinking and sustained thought: the posteriorly arisen...
Aggregates without applied thought and without sustained thought, together with sustained thought, are related to this prenascent body by way of postnascence condition.

States consisting of applied thought and sustained thought, and states without applied thought and without sustained thought, are related to a state without applied thought and without sustained thought by way of postnascence condition—
the postnascent aggregates consisting of applied thought and sustained thought, together with sustained thought, [are related] to this prenascent body.
Condition by way of posteriority condition (*pacchājātapaccaya*).

States that are both with applied thought and sustained thought (*savitakkasavicāra*) and without applied thought but with sustained thought (*avitakkavicāramatta*) are related to a state without applied thought and sustained thought (*avitakkaavicāra*) by way of posteriority condition—
the aggregates together with applied thought that have arisen posteriorly, and applied thought itself, are related to this body that has arisen prior to them by way of posteriority condition.
It is a condition by way of posteriority-condition.
A state with applied thought and sustained thought is a condition for a state with applied thought and sustained thought by way of repetition-condition— the preceding [states].

The preceding aggregates with applied thought and sustained thought are a condition for the succeeding successive aggregates with applied thought and sustained thought by way of the condition of repetition (*āsevanapaccaya*).

Adaptation (*anuloma*) is a condition for change-of-lineage (*gotrabhū*) by way of the condition of repetition; adaptation is a condition for purification (*vodāna*) by way of the condition of repetition; change-of-lineage is a condition for the path with applied thought and sustained thought by way of the condition of repetition; purification is a condition for the path with applied thought and sustained thought by way of the condition of repetition.
A state with applied thought and sustained thought is a condition for a state without applied thought but with sustained thought by way of the condition of repetition (*āsevanapaccaya*):
preceding aggregates with applied thought and sustained thought are a condition for subsequent applied thought by way of the condition of repetition;
the preliminary work (*parikamma*) for jhāna without applied thought but with sustained thought is [a condition] for jhāna without applied thought but with sustained thought.

Conditioned by way of repetition-condition (*āsevanapaccaya*): the change-of-lineage (*gotrabhū*) is a condition by way of repetition-condition for the path that is without initial application but with sustained application;
purification (*vodāna*) is a condition by way of repetition-condition for the path that is without initial application but with sustained application.
A state with both initial and sustained application is a condition by way of repetition-condition for a state without initial application and without sustained application—the second [moment].
The preparation for the first jhāna is a condition for sustained thought (vicāra) in the second jhāna by way of the condition of repetition (āsevanapaccaya).

The preparation for the third jhāna is [a condition] for the third jhāna …pe… the preparation for the fourth jhāna is [a condition] for the fourth jhāna …pe… the preparation for the base of infinite space is [a condition] for the base of infinite space …pe… [the preparation for] the base of infinite consciousness.
The preparation for the base of infinite consciousness... [and so on] ...the preparation for the base of nothingness is the base of nothingness...
[and so on] ...the preparation for the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception is the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception...
[and so on] ...the preparation for the divine eye is the divine eye... [and so on] ...the preparation for the divine ear-element is the divine ear-element.

The preparation for the ear-element … the preparation for the knowledge of the modes of supernormal power … the preparation for the knowledge of penetration of minds … the preparation for the knowledge of recollection of past lives … the preparation for the knowledge of the passing away and rebirth of beings according to their kamma … the preparation for the knowledge of the future … the change-of-lineage for the path without applied thought and sustained thought,
and for sustained thought … the purification for the [path] without applied thought and sustained thought.
It is a condition for the path and for investigation by way of the condition of repetition (*āsevanapaccaya*).

A state with applied thought and sustained thought (*savitakkasavicāra*) is a condition for a state without applied thought but with sustained thought (*avitakkavicāramatta*) and for a state without applied thought and sustained thought (*avitakka-avicāra*) by way of the condition of repetition—
the preliminary work (*parikamma*) for jhāna without applied thought but with sustained thought [is a condition] for jhāna without applied thought but with sustained thought...

Jhāna is related to sustained thought (vicāra) by way of the condition of repetition (āsevanapaccaya). Change-of-lineage (gotrabhū) is related to the path without initial application but with sustained application (avitakkavicāramatta), and to sustained thought, by way of the condition of repetition.
Purification (vodāna) is related to the path without initial application but with sustained application, and to sustained thought, by way of the condition of repetition.

A state with both initial and sustained application (savitakkasavicāra) is related to a state with both initial and sustained application, and to a state without initial application but with sustained application, [by way of the condition of repetition].

Condition by way of repetition-condition: preceding aggregates with applied thought and sustained thought are a condition, by way of repetition-condition, for subsequent aggregates with applied thought and sustained thought, and for applied thought;

adaptation is a condition for change-of-lineage and for applied thought; adaptation is a condition for purification and for applied thought; and change-of-lineage is a condition for [aggregates] with applied thought and sustained thought.

The purification of the path and of applied thought is a condition, by way of repetition-condition (*āsevanapaccaya*), for the path accompanied by applied thought and sustained thought, and for applied thought.
A state without applied thought but with sustained thought is a condition, by way of repetition-condition, for a state without applied thought but with sustained thought:
each preceding applied thought is a condition, by way of repetition-condition, for each subsequent applied thought. The preceding...

Preceding aggregates consisting of non-thinking and mere sustained thought are a condition for subsequent, successive aggregates consisting of non-thinking and mere sustained thought by way of the condition of repetition (*āsevanapaccaya*).
A state consisting of non-thinking and mere sustained thought is a condition for a state accompanied by both thinking and sustained thought by way of the condition of repetition— preceding...

A preceding applied thought (*vitakka*) is related to each subsequent aggregate accompanied by both applied and sustained thought (*savitakka-savicāra*) by way of the condition of repetition (*āsevanapaccaya*).

A state without applied thought but with sustained thought alone (*avitakka-vicāramatta*) is related to a state without both applied and sustained thought (*avitakka-avicāra*) by way of the condition of repetition:
each preceding aggregate without applied thought but with sustained thought alone is related to each subsequent sustained thought by way of the condition of repetition.

A state consisting of sustained thought without applied thought is a condition, by way of repetition-condition (*āsevanapaccaya*), for a state that consists of sustained thought without applied thought and for a state that is without both applied and sustained thought:
preceding aggregates consisting of sustained thought without applied thought are a condition,
by way of repetition-condition, for subsequent aggregates consisting of sustained thought without applied thought and for sustained thought.

A state consisting of non-initial application and sustained application is a condition, by way of the condition of repetition (*āsevanapaccaya*), for states with both initial and sustained application and states consisting of non-initial application and sustained application:

each preceding initial application is a condition, by way of the condition of repetition, for each succeeding aggregate accompanied by both initial and sustained application, as well as for the initial application itself.

A state without applied thought and without sustained thought is a condition, by way of the condition of repetition (*āsevanapaccaya*), for a state without applied thought and without sustained thought:
each preceding sustained thought is a condition, by way of the condition of repetition, for each subsequent sustained thought;
and each preceding aggregate without applied thought and without sustained thought is a condition for each subsequent aggregate without applied thought and without sustained thought.
Conditioned by way of repetition:
a state without applied thought and without sustained thought is a condition, by way of repetition, for a state without applied thought but with sustained thought.
Each preceding instance of sustained thought is a condition, by way of repetition, for each succeeding aggregate that is without applied thought but with sustained thought.

A state without applied thought and without sustained thought is a condition, by way of repetition-condition, for a state without applied thought but with sustained thought and for a state without applied thought and without sustained thought:

each preceding sustained thought is a condition, by way of repetition-condition, for each succeeding aggregate without applied thought but with sustained thought, and for the sustained thought itself.
States that are without applied thought but with sustained thought, and states that are without applied thought and without sustained thought,

are related to a state without applied thought but with sustained thought by way of the condition of repetition (āsevanapaccaya): preceding aggregates without applied thought but with sustained thought, together with sustained thought,
are related to succeeding aggregates without applied thought but with sustained thought by way of the condition of repetition.

States that are without applied thought but with sustained thought, and states that are without applied thought and without sustained thought, are related to a state without applied thought and without sustained thought by way of the condition of repetition (āsevanapaccaya)—
namely, preceding aggregates accompanied by sustained thought alone, together with the sustained thought itself,
are related to succeeding sustained thoughts by way of the condition of repetition.

States that are without applied thought but with sustained thought, and states that are without applied thought and without sustained thought, are related to states that are without applied thought but with sustained thought,
and states that are without applied thought and without sustained thought, by way of the condition of repetition (*āsevanapaccaya*):

preceding aggregates without applied thought but with sustained thought, together with sustained thought, are related to succeeding aggregates without applied thought but with sustained thought, and to sustained thought.
Conditioned by way of repetition-condition (āsevanapaccaya):

states that are both with applied thought and sustained thought (savitakkasavicāra) and without applied thought but with sustained thought only (avitakkavicāramatta) are conditions, by way of repetition-condition, for a state that is with applied thought and sustained thought.
Namely, preceding aggregates with applied thought and sustained thought, together with applied thought itself, are conditions for succeeding [aggregates].
It is a condition for subsequent aggregates with applied thought and sustained thought by way of repetition-condition (*āsevanapaccaya*).
Adaptation (*anuloma*) and applied thought are conditions for change-of-lineage (*gotrabhū*); adaptation and applied thought are conditions for purification (*vodāna*);

change-of-lineage and applied thought are conditions for the path with applied thought and sustained thought; and purification and applied thought are conditions for the path with applied thought and sustained thought.
Conditioned by the relation of repetition (āsevanapaccaya):

states that are both with applied thought and sustained thought (savitakkasavicāra) and without applied thought but with sustained thought only (avitakkavicāramatta) are related to a state without applied thought but with sustained thought only by way of the relation of repetition—
the preceding aggregates together with applied thought (vitakka), which are both with applied thought and sustained thought, [are related] to the succeeding [state].

The subsequent thought-moment is a condition for the preceding one by way of repetition-condition (*āsevanapaccaya*). Both the preliminary work (*parikamma*) and the thought-moment of a jhāna that is without applied thought but with sustained thought (*avitakkavicāramatta*) are conditions for that same jhāna by way of repetition-condition.

Both the change-of-lineage (*gotrabhū*) and the thought-moment are conditions for the path without applied thought but with sustained thought; both the purification (*vodāna*) and the thought-moment are conditions for the path without applied thought but with sustained thought.
It is a condition for the Path by way of the condition of repetition (*āsevanapaccaya*).

States with applied thought and sustained thought (*savitakkasavicāra*) and states without applied thought but with sustained thought (*avitakkavicāramatta*) are conditions for a state without applied thought and sustained thought by way of the condition of repetition—

the preliminary work (*parikamma*) and the applied thought (*vitakka*) for the second jhāna are conditions for the sustained thought (*vicāra*) in the second jhāna by way of the condition of repetition.
Condition ... pe ... the preliminary work and applied thought for the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception ... pe ... the preliminary work and applied thought for the divine eye ... pe ...
the preliminary work and applied thought for the knowledge of future lives are related to the knowledge of future lives by way of repetition-condition (*āsevana-paccaya*).
The change-of-lineage (*gotrabhū*) and applied thought are related to the path without applied thought and sustained thought, and to sustained thought ... pe ... by way of repetition-condition.

And [these] are related by way of the condition of repetition (*āsevanapaccaya*). Both purification (*vodāna*) and applied thought (*vitakka*) are related by way of the condition of repetition to the path that is without applied thought and sustained thought (*avitakkavicāra*), and to sustained thought (*vicāra*).

Phenomena that possess both applied and sustained thought (*savitakkasavicāra*) and those that possess sustained thought but are without applied thought (*avitakkavicāramatta*) are related to [phenomena] that possess sustained thought but are without applied thought and to those that are without both applied and sustained thought (*avitakkavicāra*).

And a state is related to a state by way of the condition of repetition: the preparation for a jhāna that is without applied thought but with sustained thought (*avitakkavicāramatta*), as well as applied thought itself, are related to that jhāna without applied thought but with sustained thought and to its sustained thought;

likewise, change-of-lineage (*gotrabhū*) and applied thought are related to the path without applied thought but with sustained thought and to its sustained thought; and purification (*vodāna*) and applied thought are related to [the path] without applied thought but with sustained thought...
It is a condition for the path and for sustained thought by way of the condition of repetition (*āsevanapaccaya*).

States with applied thought and sustained thought (*savitakkasavicāra*) and states without applied thought but with sustained thought (*avitakkavicāramatta*) are conditions for states with applied thought and sustained thought and states without applied thought but with sustained thought by way of the condition of repetition—
the preceding aggregates with applied thought and sustained thought, and...
Applied thought (vitakka) is a condition by way of repetition for subsequent aggregates accompanied by applied and sustained thought, and for applied thought itself.
Adaptation (anuloma) and applied thought are conditions for change-of-lineage (gotrabhū) and applied thought;

adaptation and applied thought are conditions for purification (vodāna) and applied thought; and change-of-lineage and applied thought are conditions for [subsequent states] accompanied by applied and sustained thought.
The purification and the applied thought are related to the path with applied and sustained thought and to that applied thought by way of the condition of repetition.
(Kamma)
A state with applied thought and sustained thought is a condition, by way of kamma-condition, for a state with applied thought and sustained thought—either as co-nascent or at different moments.
As co-nascent: volition with applied thought and sustained thought is a condition, by way of kamma-condition, for the associated aggregates.
At the moment of rebirth-linking, volition with applied thought and sustained thought is a condition, by way of kamma-condition, for the associated aggregates.

Condition. As asynchronous: volition accompanied by applied thought and sustained thought is a condition, by way of kamma-condition, for resultant aggregates accompanied by applied thought and sustained thought.
A state accompanied by applied thought and sustained thought is a condition, by way of kamma-condition, for a state without applied thought but with sustained thought—conascent.

[Conditioned by] volition with applied thought and sustained thought at different times. As conascent: volition with applied thought and sustained thought is a condition for applied thought by way of kamma-condition.
At the moment of rebirth-linking: volition with applied thought and sustained thought is a condition for applied thought by way of kamma-condition. As at different times:
volition with applied thought and sustained thought is a condition for resultant applied thought by way of kamma-condition.

A state with applied thought and sustained thought (*savitakkasavicāra*) is a condition for a state without applied thought and sustained thought (*avitakka-avicāra*) by way of kamma-condition (*kammapaccaya*):

namely, co-nascent (*sahajāta*) and asynchronous (*nānākkhaṇika*). Co-nascent: Volition accompanied by applied and sustained thought is a kamma-condition for mind-produced matter (*cittasamuṭṭhāna-rūpa*).
At the moment of rebirth-linking (*paṭisandhi*), volition accompanied by applied and sustained thought is a kamma-condition for kamma-born matter (*kaṭattā-rūpa*).

Condition. Asynchronous: volition accompanied by applied thought and sustained thought is a condition, by way of kamma-condition, for resultant aggregates devoid of applied thought and sustained thought, and for the matter produced by kamma (kaṭattā-rūpa).

A state accompanied by applied thought and sustained thought is [a condition] for a state both accompanied by applied thought and sustained thought and devoid of applied thought and sustained thought.
Condition by way of kamma-condition: [it is] co-nascent and asynchronous. Co-nascent:

volition accompanied by initial application and sustained application is a condition by way of kamma-condition for its associated aggregates and for mind-produced matter. At the moment of rebirth-linking, volition accompanied by initial application and sustained application is a condition by way of kamma-condition for its associated aggregates and for kamma-born matter.

Condition. Asynchronous: Volition accompanied by applied thought and sustained thought is a condition, by way of kamma-condition, for resultant aggregates accompanied by applied thought and sustained thought, and for the matter produced by kamma (kaṭattā-rūpa).

A state accompanied by applied thought and sustained thought [is a condition] for a state without applied thought but with sustained thought, and for a state without applied thought and without sustained thought.
Condition by way of kamma-condition: [it is] conascent and asynchronous. Conascent:

volition accompanied by applied thought and sustained thought is a condition by way of kamma-condition for applied thought and for mind-produced matter. At the moment of rebirth-linking, volition accompanied by applied thought and sustained thought is a condition by way of kamma-condition for applied thought and for kamma-wrought matter.

Various asynchronous [conditions]: volition accompanied by applied thought and sustained thought is a condition, by way of kamma-condition, for resultant applied thought and for the material phenomena produced by that kamma.

A state accompanied by applied thought and sustained thought is a condition for a state accompanied by applied thought and sustained thought and for a state without applied thought but with sustained thought.
Condition by way of kamma-condition: [it is] co-nascent and asynchronous. Co-nascent:

volition accompanied by applied thought and sustained thought is a condition by way of kamma-condition for its associated aggregates and for applied thought. At the moment of rebirth-linking, volition accompanied by applied thought and sustained thought is a condition by way of kamma-condition for its associated aggregates and for applied thought.

Condition. Asynchronous: Volition accompanied by applied thought and sustained thought (*savitakkasavicārā cetanā*) is a condition, by way of kamma-condition (*kammapaccaya*), for resultant aggregates accompanied by applied thought and sustained thought, as well as for applied thought.

A state accompanied by applied thought and sustained thought is a condition for [states] accompanied by applied thought and sustained thought, for those without applied thought but with sustained thought alone (*avitakkavicāramatta*), and for those without applied thought and sustained thought (*avitakka-avicāra*).
And it is a condition for the dhamma by way of kamma-condition—both co-nascent and asynchronous. Co-nascent:
volition accompanied by initial application and sustained application is a condition by way of kamma-condition for its associated aggregates, for initial application, and for mind-produced matter.
At the moment of rebirth-linking, volition accompanied by initial application and sustained application [is a condition] for its associated aggregates and for initial application...
And volition is a condition for past and future material phenomena by way of kamma-condition. As asynchronous (nānākkhaṇika):

volition accompanied by initial application and sustained application is a condition for resultant aggregates accompanied by initial application and sustained application, as well as for initial application and past and future material phenomena, by way of kamma-condition.

A state without initial application but with sustained application is a condition for a state without initial application but with sustained application by way of kamma-condition—as conascent (sahajāta).
[Asynchronous. Co-nascent: volition consisting of non-initial application and sustained application is a condition by way of kamma-condition for its associated aggregates.

At the moment of rebirth-linking … [etc. … Asynchronous: volition consisting of non-initial application and sustained application is a condition by way of kamma-condition for resultant aggregates consisting of non-initial application and sustained application.

A state with applied thought but sustained thought (*avitakkavicāramatta*) is a condition, by way of kamma-condition (*kammapaccaya*), for a state without applied thought and sustained thought (*avitakka-avicāra*).

This is twofold: conascent (*sahajāta*) and asynchronous (*nānākkhaṇika*). As conascent: volition with applied thought but sustained thought is a condition, by way of kamma-condition, for sustained thought and for mind-produced matter (*cittasamuṭṭhāna-rūpa*).
At the moment of rebirth-linking (*paṭisandhi*), volition with applied thought but sustained thought is a condition for resultant [states].
Volition associated with sustained thought (*vicāra*) is a condition for sustained thought and for material phenomena through the condition of kamma. As asynchronous:
volition without applied thought but with sustained thought (*avitakkavicāramatta*) is a condition for resultant sustained thought and for material phenomena through the condition of kamma.

A state without applied thought but with sustained thought is a condition for a state without applied thought but with sustained thought and for a state without applied thought and without sustained thought.
Condition by way of kamma-condition: [it is] co-nascent and asynchronous. Co-nascent:
volition without applied thought but with sustained thought is a condition by way of kamma-condition for its associated aggregates, for sustained thought, and for mind-produced matter.
At the moment of rebirth-linking, volition without applied thought but with sustained thought [is a condition] for its associated aggregates and for sustained thought...

And volition is a condition for the resultant aggregates accompanied by sustained thought but without applied thought, for sustained thought, and for the bodily form produced by karma (*kaṭattā-rūpa*), by way of the kamma-condition. As asynchronous:

volition accompanied by sustained thought but without applied thought is a condition for the resultant aggregates accompanied by sustained thought but without applied thought, for sustained thought, and for the bodily form produced by karma, by way of the kamma-condition.
A state without applied thought and without sustained thought is a condition for a state without applied thought and without sustained thought by way of the kamma-condition—as co-nascent.

[This is] of different moments. As conascent: volition without applied thought and sustained thought is a condition, by way of kamma-condition, for its associated aggregates and for mind-produced matter.

At the moment of rebirth-linking: volition without applied thought and sustained thought is a condition, by way of kamma-condition, for its associated aggregates and for kamma-born matter. [As] of different moments: volition without applied thought and sustained thought...
Volition is a condition, by way of kamma-condition, for resultant aggregates that are without applied thought and sustained thought, and for the matter produced by kamma.
Resultant state with applied thought and sustained thought is a condition, by way of resultant-condition, for a state with applied thought and sustained thought— namely, the resultant [state].

One aggregate accompanied by initial application and sustained application is a condition for three aggregates by way of resultant condition … at the moment of rebirth-linking, one aggregate accompanied by initial application and sustained application is a condition for three aggregates by way of resultant condition … A state accompanied by initial application and sustained application is a condition for a state without initial application but with sustained application by way of resultant condition: resultant aggregates accompanied by initial application and sustained application are a condition for initial application by way of resultant condition. At the moment of rebirth-linking … pe … [end].
(The seven questions based on "with applied thought and sustained thought" are complete.
A state without applied thought but with sustained thought is a condition, by way of resultant condition, for a state without applied thought but with sustained thought:
one resultant aggregate without applied thought but with sustained thought is a condition, by way of resultant condition, for three aggregates … pe … [and so forth].
Two aggregates ... [etc. ... at the moment of rebirth-linking, one resultant aggregate that is without applied thought but with sustained thought ... [etc. ...
(Five questions should be formulated based on "without applied thought but with sustained thought," specifying "resultant.

A state without applied thought and without sustained thought is a condition, by way of resultant condition, for a state without applied thought and without sustained thought: [namely,] a resultant ...

One aggregate without applied thought and sustained thought is a condition, by way of resultant condition, for three aggregates and for mind-produced matter … two aggregates … [and so on] … Resultant sustained thought is a condition, by way of resultant condition, for mind-produced matter.
At the moment of rebirth-linking … aggregates are a condition, by way of resultant condition, for the physical basis. Sustained thought … [is a condition for mind-produced matter].
A state without applied thought and sustained thought is related to a state with applied thought and sustained thought by way of resultant condition.
A resultant sustained thought is related to the aggregates with applied thought and sustained thought by way of resultant condition. At the moment of rebirth-linking...

Resultant sustained thought (*vicāra*) is a condition, by way of resultant condition (*vipākapaccaya*), for the aggregates that possess sustained thought but lack applied thought (*avitakkavicāramatta*).

A state without applied thought and without sustained thought is a condition, by way of resultant condition, for a state without applied thought and with sustained thought, and for a state without applied thought and without sustained thought:
namely, resultant sustained thought is a condition for the aggregates that possess sustained thought but lack applied thought and for mind-produced matter (*cittasamuṭṭhāna*).

[Resultant states] are related to material phenomena by way of resultant condition. At the moment of rebirth-linking, resultant sustained thought is related to the aggregates without applied thought but with sustained thought and to the kamma-produced material phenomena by way of resultant condition.

States that are without applied thought but with sustained thought and without applied thought and sustained thought are related to a state without applied thought but with sustained thought... [by way of resultant condition].

Condition by way of resultant condition: one resultant aggregate accompanied by sustained thought but without applied thought, together with sustained thought, is a condition by way of resultant condition for three aggregates … two aggregates … [and so on] … at the moment of rebirth-linking … [and so on].

States that are both without applied thought and accompanied by sustained thought, and states that are without applied thought and without sustained thought, are conditions by way of resultant condition for a state that is without applied thought and without sustained thought.
Condition: Resultant aggregates accompanied by sustained thought but without applied thought, together with sustained thought, are related to mind-produced matter by way of resultant condition.

At the moment of rebirth-linking, aggregates accompanied by sustained thought but without applied thought, together with sustained thought, are related to kamma-produced matter by way of resultant condition.

States that are without applied thought but with sustained thought, and states that are without applied thought and without sustained thought, are related to states that are without applied thought but with sustained thought, and states that are without applied thought and without sustained thought, by way of resultant condition (*vipākapaccaya*).

For example: one resultant aggregate accompanied by sustained thought and sustained thought itself are related to the other three aggregates and to mind-produced matter by way of resultant condition …pe….
At the moment of rebirth-linking, one resultant aggregate accompanied by sustained thought but without applied thought, together with sustained thought itself,
is a condition for the three aggregates and for the kamma-produced matter by way of resultant condition (*vipākapaccaya*).

Phenomena that are both with applied and sustained thought, and those that are without applied thought but with sustained thought, [are conditions] for a phenomenon with both applied and sustained thought.

Condition by way of resultant condition: one resultant aggregate accompanied by applied thought and sustained thought, together with applied thought, is a condition by way of resultant condition for three aggregates … two aggregates … [and so on] … at the moment of rebirth-linking … [and so on].

States accompanied by applied thought and sustained thought, and states without applied thought but with sustained thought, are conditions by way of resultant condition for a state without applied thought and without sustained thought.
Condition: Resultant aggregates accompanied by applied thought and sustained thought, together with applied thought itself, are related to mind-produced matter by way of resultant condition.

At the moment of rebirth-linking … [and so forth] … States accompanied by applied thought and sustained thought, as well as those without applied thought but with sustained thought alone, are related to states accompanied by applied thought and sustained thought, and to those without applied thought and sustained thought.

And [this] state is a condition for [those] states by way of resultant condition: one resultant aggregate accompanied by applied thought and sustained thought, together with applied thought, is a condition for the three aggregates and for mind-produced matter by way of resultant condition. At the moment of rebirth-linking …pe… nutriment.

A state with applied thought and sustained thought (*savitakkasavicāra*) is a condition for a state with applied thought and sustained thought by way of nutriment-condition (*āhārapaccaya*): nutriments with applied thought and sustained thought are a condition by way of nutriment-condition for the associated aggregates. At the moment of rebirth-linking (*paṭisandhi*) … [etc.

At the moment of rebirth-linking … [etc. …

nutriments without applied thought but with sustained thought are a condition, by way of nutriment-condition, for the associated aggregates. At the moment of rebirth-linking … pe … [end as above].
A state consisting of sustained thought without applied thought is a condition, by way of nutriment-condition, for a state without applied thought and sustained thought:

nutriments consisting of sustained thought without applied thought are a condition, by way of nutriment-condition, for sustained thought and for the material phenomena produced by consciousness. At the moment of rebirth-linking … [etc.

… A state consisting of sustained thought without applied thought is a condition, by way of nutriment-condition, for a state consisting of sustained thought without applied thought and for a state without applied thought and sustained thought.

Condition by way of nutriment-condition: nutriments accompanied by sustained thought but without applied thought are a condition by way of nutriment-condition for their associated aggregates, for sustained thought, and for mind-produced matter. At the moment of rebirth-linking ... [etc. ...

A state without applied thought and without sustained thought is a condition by way of nutriment-condition for a state without applied thought and without sustained thought: [nutriments] without applied thought and without sustained thought...
Nutriments are a condition, by way of nutriment-condition, for the associated aggregates and for mind-produced matter.
At the moment of rebirth-linking … [and so on] … Edible food is a condition, by way of nutriment-condition, for this body.
Faculty … [condition].
A state with applied thought and sustained thought (*savitakkasavicāra*) is a condition for a state with applied thought and sustained thought by way of faculty-condition (*indriya-paccaya*).

The faculties with applied thought and sustained thought are a condition, by way of faculty-condition, for the associated aggregates (*khandha*). At the moment of rebirth-linking (*paṭisandhi*)... [etc.]...

A state with applied thought and sustained thought is a condition for a state without applied thought but with sustained thought (*avitakkavicāramatta*) by way of faculty-condition. The faculties with applied thought and sustained thought are a condition, by way of faculty-condition, for applied thought (*vitakka*). At the moment of rebirth-linking... [etc.]...

A state without applied thought but with sustained thought is a condition, by way of faculty-condition, for a state without applied thought but with sustained thought:
faculties without applied thought but with sustained thought are a condition, by way of faculty-condition, for the associated aggregates. At the moment of rebirth-linking ... pe ... [end as above].
A state with applied thought but without sustained thought is a condition, by way of faculty-condition, for a state without applied thought and without sustained thought:

the faculties with applied thought but without sustained thought are a condition, by way of faculty-condition, for sustained thought and for mind-produced matter. At the moment of rebirth-linking ... [etc.

... A state with applied thought but without sustained thought is a condition for a state with applied thought but without sustained thought and for a state without applied thought and without sustained thought.

Condition by way of faculty-condition (*indriya-paccaya*): The faculties devoid of applied thought but accompanied by sustained thought (*avitakka-vicāramatta*) are related to their associated aggregates, to sustained thought, and to mind-produced matter by way of faculty-condition. At the moment of rebirth-linking (*paṭisandhi-kkhaṇe*) ... [etc. ...

A state devoid of both applied and sustained thought (*avitakka-avicāra*) is related to a state devoid of both applied and sustained thought by way of faculty-condition: the [faculties] devoid of both applied and sustained thought...
The faculties are related to their associated aggregates and to mind-produced matter by way of faculty condition.
At the moment of rebirth-linking ... [etc] ... the eye-faculty is related to eye-consciousness ... [etc] ... the body-faculty is related to body-consciousness by way of faculty condition.
The material life-faculty is related to kamma-produced matter by way of faculty condition.
Jhāna:

A state with applied thought and sustained thought (savitakkasavicāra) is a condition, by way of jhāna-condition, for a state with applied thought and sustained thought—the jhāna factors with applied thought and sustained thought are a condition, by way of jhāna-condition, for the associated aggregates. At the moment of rebirth-linking … pe … [end].
(The seven questions rooted in "with applied thought and sustained thought" are to be analyzed by this same method.
A state without applied thought but with sustained thought is a condition, by way of jhāna-condition, for a state without applied thought but with sustained thought:

jhāna-factors without applied thought but with sustained thought are a condition, by way of jhāna-condition, for the associated aggregates. At the moment of rebirth-linking ... pe ... [same as above].
(The five questions rooted in "without applied thought and with sustained thought" should be analyzed by this same method.
A state without applied thought and without sustained thought is a condition, by way of the jhāna-condition, for a state without applied thought and without sustained thought:
the jhāna factors without applied thought and without sustained thought are a condition, by way of the jhāna-condition, for their associated aggregates and for mind-produced matter.

Condition: Sustained thought (*vicāra*) is a condition for mind-produced matter by way of the jhāna-condition. At the moment of rebirth-linking, sustained thought is a condition for kamma-produced matter by way of the jhāna-condition. Sustained thought is a condition for the physical base by way of the jhāna-condition.
A state without applied thought and without sustained thought is a condition for a state with applied thought and sustained thought-only by way of the jhāna-condition—namely, sustained thought.

Aggregates accompanied by sustained thought but devoid of applied thought are related to aggregates accompanied by sustained thought but devoid of applied thought by way of the jhāna condition. At the moment of rebirth-linking, sustained thought is related to aggregates accompanied by sustained thought but devoid of applied thought by way of the jhāna condition.

A state devoid of both applied and sustained thought is related to a state accompanied by sustained thought but devoid of applied thought and to a state devoid of both applied and sustained thought [by way of the jhāna condition].
Condition by way of jhāna: sustained thought (vicāra) is a condition by way of jhāna for aggregates devoid of applied thought but possessed of sustained thought, and for mind-produced matter.
At the moment of rebirth-linking, sustained thought is a condition by way of jhāna for aggregates devoid of applied thought but possessed of sustained thought, and for kamma-produced matter.

States that are without applied thought but with sustained thought, and states that are without applied thought and without sustained thought, are related to a state without applied thought but with sustained thought by way of the condition of jhāna:
the jhāna-factors without applied thought but with sustained thought, and sustained thought, are related to their associated aggregates by way of the condition of jhāna.
At the moment of rebirth-linking … pe … [end].

States consisting of sustained thought without applied thought, and states without both applied and sustained thought, are related to a state without both applied and sustained thought by way of the condition of jhāna:
jhāna-factors consisting of sustained thought without applied thought, and sustained thought, are related to mind-produced matter by way of the condition of jhāna.
